CLAUDE.md:1311:## Environment notes
"""Auto zone: which State Plane zone a latitude/longitude falls in, by county.

**The rule is the law's, not a geometry of this program's choosing**
(docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md L3). Both Michigan systems are unions of whole
counties, and Michigan's counties extend into the Great Lakes:

* SPCS 83: MCL 54.231(3)-(5) defines each zone as "the area included in the
  following counties" (``michspc.spc.autozone_spcs83``).
* SPCS2022: NGS's eighteen low-distortion zones are unions of Census TIGER
  county lines, measured to 0.026 m, with one split - Keweenaw County's Isle
  Royale is its own zone (``michspc.spc.autozone_spcs2022``). The statewide
  zone 260001 is never chosen (owner's decision, plan section 1 item 2).

So a position is assigned by finding the ONE county polygon it lies in and
reading that county's zone from the system's table. A position in no county is
refused by name (L5): never the nearest zone, never a guess.

**Stdlib only, no file I/O** (tests/test_architecture.py). The polygons are
handed in as ``County`` records, already read and authenticated by
``michspc.fileio.counties`` - the only reader of the shipped county file.

Coordinates: decimal degrees, **longitude negative west**, as everywhere in
this codebase (docs/DESIGN.md section 7). A polygon vertex is
``(longitude, latitude)``, the order the county file stores it. Point-in-polygon
is planar on (longitude, latitude): the county lines are straight segments
between vertices TIGER publishes densely (72,545 for Michigan), and the
difference between a straight segment in degrees and a geodesic is far below
the source's own positional uncertainty (RECON.md section 4).

The point-in-polygon rule
-------------------------

**Even-odd crossing count over every ring of the county** - outer rings, holes
and islands alike, with no orientation needed - casting a ray due east from the
point. An edge between two vertices counts as crossed when

    y_low <= latitude < y_high   and   longitude < x_at(latitude)

where the edge's endpoints are first put in a canonical order (the one with the
smaller latitude first, longitude breaking a tie) and ``x_at`` is evaluated from
that canonical order. Horizontal edges never count.

Two consequences, both deliberate:

* **Deterministic on a line.** A point exactly on a county line belongs to the
  county it would be in after an infinitesimal step EAST; if it is still on a
  line after that (the line runs exactly east-west), after a further
  infinitesimally smaller step NORTH. So a point on a north-south line goes to
  the county east of it, a point on an east-west line to the county north of
  it, and a point exactly on a corner where four counties meet goes to the
  north-east one. This is the half-open crossing rule; it is written down
  because MCL 54.234 permits either zone for a tract on a line and leaves a
  point exactly on it undefined (RECON.md section 3), and this program must
  still give one answer, the same every time.
* **One county, not two.** Adjacent counties store a shared line with the same
  vertices (TIGER is topological: every one of Michigan's 41,591 county edges
  is used by exactly one county, on the state's outline, or by exactly two).
  Because the crossing test is computed from the canonical order, both counties
  evaluate the shared edge to the bit-identical crossing decision, and the
  point falls on one side of it for both. Even so, ``zone_for`` does not rely on
  that: it tests EVERY candidate county and refuses a point that two counties
  both claim, rather than picking one.

Speed: each county keeps its bounding box (the prefilter) and its edges binned
by latitude, so a point is tested only against the few edges whose latitude
span covers it. ``tests/test_autozone.py`` holds the binned search equal to the
plain all-edges count, and measures the time.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Iterable, Mapping

from michspc.spc import autozone_spcs83, autozone_spcs2022
from michspc.spc.zones import SPCS83_ZONES, SPCS2022_ZONES, Zone

Vertex = tuple[float, float]
"""``(longitude, latitude)``, decimal degrees, longitude negative west."""

Ring = tuple[Vertex, ...]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refusals.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class AutoZoneRefusal(Exception):
    """Base class for every refusal in this module.

    A caller that only needs "Auto could not choose a zone for this point, say
    why" catches this. The subclasses separate what a surveyor is told
    differently. Carries the refused position as data (``latitude``,
    ``longitude``; decimal degrees, negative west) so a caller that knows which
    point of a file it was can name it in its own words; both are None on a
    refusal that is not about a position (a malformed county set).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        latitude: float | None = None,
        longitude: float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.latitude = latitude
        self.longitude = longitude


class AutoZoneInputError(AutoZoneRefusal):
    """A latitude, longitude or system that is not a usable value."""


class AutoZoneOutsideError(AutoZoneRefusal):
    """The position is in no Michigan county, land or Great Lakes water."""


class AutoZoneAmbiguousError(AutoZoneRefusal):
    """Two or more county polygons both contain the position.

    Never resolved by picking one: it would mean the county data overlaps, and
    the zone would then depend on the order the counties were tested in. The
    shipped data has no overlap (tested); this refusal is the guard for the day
    a re-derived file does.
    """


class AutoZoneDataError(AutoZoneRefusal):
    """The county records or the zone tables are inconsistent with each other."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The system an Auto zone is chosen in.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class AutoZoneSystem(Enum):
    """Which State Plane system Auto chooses a zone in.

    The values are the registry's own ``Zone.system`` strings, so a chosen
    zone's system can be checked against the system asked for by equality.
    """

    SPCS83 = "SPCS 83"
    SPCS2022 = "SPCS2022"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ZoneAssignment:
    """The zone Auto chose for one position, and the county that decided it.

    ``zone`` is a record from ``michspc.spc.zones`` itself, by identity - never
    a copy - so every fact about the zone (constants, units, frame) is the
    registry's.
    """

    zone: Zone
    county_name: str
    """TIGER's county name, e.g. "St. Clair" (the county file's NAME field)."""

    county_fips: str
    """The five-digit county FIPS code, state 26 first, e.g. "26147"."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# County polygons.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class County:
    """One county's polygon, as the county file stores it.

    ``rings`` are every ring of the county's polygon - outer boundaries, holes
    and islands alike, in the file's order - each a closed sequence of
    ``(longitude, latitude)`` vertices whose last vertex repeats its first.
    The even-odd rule needs no ring to be marked as a hole.
    """

    fips: str
    name: str
    rings: tuple[Ring, ...]


_Edge = tuple[float, float, float, float]
"""A non-horizontal edge in canonical order: (x_low, y_low, x_high, y_high),
y_low < y_high."""


def _canonical_edges(rings: Iterable[Ring]) -> list[_Edge]:
    """Every non-horizontal edge of every ring, lower endpoint first.

    The canonical order is what makes the crossing decision for an edge shared
    by two counties bit-identical in both: each county may walk that edge in
    the opposite direction, and without the reordering the interpolated
    crossing longitude would be computed from the endpoints in two different
    orders and could differ in its last bit.
    """
    edges: list[_Edge] = []
    for ring in rings:
        for (xa, ya), (xb, yb) in zip(ring[:-1], ring[1:]):
            if ya == yb:
                continue  # a horizontal edge is never crossed by an eastward ray
            if (ya, xa) < (yb, xb):
                edges.append((xa, ya, xb, yb))
            else:
                edges.append((xb, yb, xa, ya))
    return edges


def _crosses(edge: _Edge, longitude: float, latitude: float) -> bool:
    """Whether a ray due east from the point crosses this canonical edge.

    The half-open rule: the edge's lower endpoint is included and its upper one
    excluded, and a point exactly on the edge (``longitude == x``) is NOT
    counted - which is what puts a point on a line in the county east (then
    north) of it. See the module docstring.
    """
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = edge
    if not (y0 <= latitude < y1):
        return False
    x = x0 + (latitude - y0) * (x1 - x0) / (y1 - y0)
    return longitude < x


def even_odd_contains(rings: Iterable[Ring], longitude: float, latitude: float) -> bool:
    """The plain all-edges even-odd test, with no index.

    The reference the binned search in ``PreparedCounty.contains`` is held
    equal to; also usable on any polygon (the suite recomputes NGS's zone
    membership with it).
    """
    inside = False
    for edge in _canonical_edges(rings):
        if _crosses(edge, longitude, latitude):
            inside = not inside
    return inside


_EDGES_PER_BIN = 8
"""Target edges per latitude bin. A speed knob only - the result is the same
for any value, which the suite holds over random points."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PreparedCounty:
    """A county with its bounding box and its edges binned by latitude."""

    county: County
    min_longitude: float
    min_latitude: float
    max_longitude: float
    max_latitude: float
    _bin_height: float = field(repr=False)
    _bins: tuple[tuple[_Edge, ...], ...] = field(repr=False)

    @classmethod
    def build(cls, county: County) -> "PreparedCounty":
        xs = [x for ring in county.rings for x, _ in ring]
        ys = [y for ring in county.rings for _, y in ring]
        min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y = min(xs), max(xs), min(ys), max(ys)
        edges = _canonical_edges(county.rings)
        count = max(1, len(edges) // _EDGES_PER_BIN)
        height = (max_y - min_y) / count if max_y > min_y else 1.0
        bins: list[list[_Edge]] = [[] for _ in range(count)]
        for edge in edges:
            # An edge goes into every bin its latitude span touches. The bin
            # index is a monotone function of latitude (a subtraction and a
            # division by a positive constant are monotone in IEEE
            # arithmetic), so the bin a query latitude maps to always holds
            # every edge whose span contains that latitude.
            first = _bin_index(edge[1], min_y, height, count)
            last = _bin_index(edge[3], min_y, height, count)
            for k in range(first, last + 1):
                bins[k].append(edge)
        return cls(
            county=county,
            min_longitude=min_x,
            min_latitude=min_y,
            max_longitude=max_x,
            max_latitude=max_y,
            _bin_height=height,
            _bins=tuple(tuple(b) for b in bins),
        )

    def in_box(self, longitude: float, latitude: float) -> bool:
        """The prefilter. INCLUSIVE on every side: a point on the box's west
        edge can be inside the county by the on-line rule."""
        return (
            self.min_longitude <= longitude <= self.max_longitude
            and self.min_latitude <= latitude <= self.max_latitude
        )

    def contains(self, longitude: float, latitude: float) -> bool:
        if not self.in_box(longitude, latitude):
            return False
        k = _bin_index(latitude, self.min_latitude, self._bin_height, len(self._bins))
        inside = False
        for edge in self._bins[k]:
            if _crosses(edge, longitude, latitude):
                inside = not inside
        return inside


def _bin_index(latitude: float, min_latitude: float, height: float, count: int) -> int:
    k = int((latitude - min_latitude) / height)
    return 0 if k < 0 else (count - 1 if k >= count else k)


class CountySet:
    """The prepared counties ``zone_for`` searches, plus where they came from.

    Built once per process by ``michspc.fileio.counties`` (the shipped file is
    read and authenticated there) and reused for every point. ``source`` is the
    one-line description of the county data that a refusal names, e.g.
    "US Census TIGER/Line 2025 counties".
    """

    def __init__(self, counties: Iterable[County], source: str) -> None:
        prepared = []
        seen: dict[str, County] = {}
        for county in counties:
            if not isinstance(county, County):
                raise AutoZoneDataError(
                    f"A county set holds County records only; got "
                    f"{type(county).__name__} ({county!r})."
                )
            if county.fips in seen:
                raise AutoZoneDataError(
                    f"Two county records share FIPS {county.fips}: "
                    f"{seen[county.fips].name} and {county.name}. The zone "
                    f"tables are keyed by FIPS, so this would make a zone "
                    f"depend on which record was read last."
                )
            seen[county.fips] = county
            prepared.append(PreparedCounty.build(county))
        if not prepared:
            raise AutoZoneDataError("A county set must hold at least one county.")
        self._prepared: tuple[PreparedCounty, ...] = tuple(prepared)
        self.source = source

    @property
    def counties(self) -> tuple[County, ...]:
        return tuple(p.county for p in self._prepared)

    def by_fips(self, fips: str) -> County:
        for p in self._prepared:
            if p.county.fips == fips:
                return p.county
        raise KeyError(fips)

    def containing(self, longitude: float, latitude: float) -> list[County]:
        """EVERY county whose polygon contains the point, in data order."""
        return [p.county for p in self._prepared if p.contains(longitude, latitude)]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The assignment.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _require_number(value: object, what: str) -> float:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        raise AutoZoneInputError(
            f"Auto zone needs the {what} as a number of decimal degrees; got "
            f"{type(value).__name__} ({value!r})."
        )
    number = float(value)
    if not math.isfinite(number):
        raise AutoZoneInputError(
            f"Auto zone needs a finite {what}; got {value!r}."
        )
    return number


def _position_text(latitude: float, longitude: float) -> str:
    return f"latitude {latitude:.8f}, longitude {longitude:.8f}"


def zone_for(
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    system: AutoZoneSystem,
    counties: CountySet,
) -> ZoneAssignment:
    """The zone of ``system`` that the county containing the position belongs to.

    ``latitude`` and ``longitude`` are decimal degrees, **longitude negative
    west**, in the frame of the system asked for (NAD83(2011) for SPCS 83,
    NATRF2022 for SPCS2022 - plan L4; this function cannot check that, and the
    caller states it). Refuses, never guesses:

    * ``AutoZoneInputError`` - not a finite number, latitude beyond +/-90 or
      longitude beyond +/-180, or ``system`` not an ``AutoZoneSystem``;
    * ``AutoZoneOutsideError`` - in no Michigan county (outside Michigan, or in
      another state's or Canada's water). The nearest zone is never offered;
    * ``AutoZoneAmbiguousError`` - two county polygons both contain it;
    * ``AutoZoneDataError`` - the county has no row in the system's table.
    """
    lat = _require_number(latitude, "latitude")
    lon = _require_number(longitude, "longitude")
    if not -90.0 <= lat <= 90.0:
        raise AutoZoneInputError(
            f"Latitude {lat!r} is not between -90 and 90 degrees.",
            latitude=lat,
            longitude=lon,
        )
    if not -180.0 <= lon <= 180.0:
        raise AutoZoneInputError(
            f"Longitude {lon!r} is not between -180 and 180 degrees. Auto zone "
            f"takes a signed longitude, negative west.",
            latitude=lat,
            longitude=lon,
        )
    if not isinstance(system, AutoZoneSystem):
        raise AutoZoneInputError(
            f"Auto zone needs an AutoZoneSystem (SPCS83 or SPCS2022); got "
            f"{type(system).__name__} ({system!r}).",
            latitude=lat,
            longitude=lon,
        )
    if not isinstance(counties, CountySet):
        raise AutoZoneDataError(
            f"Auto zone needs the loaded CountySet; got {type(counties).__name__}.",
            latitude=lat,
            longitude=lon,
        )

    found = counties.containing(lon, lat)
    if not found:
        hint = ""
        if lon > 0.0 and counties.containing(-lon, lat):
            hint = (
                " The longitude is positive (east of Greenwich); Michigan's "
                "longitudes are negative here (negative west), and the same "
                "number negated would be inside Michigan - check the sign "
                "convention of the input."
            )
        raise AutoZoneOutsideError(
            f"The point at {_position_text(lat, lon)} is in no Michigan "
            f"county ({counties.source}, Great Lakes waters included), so "
            f"Auto cannot choose a {system.value} zone for it. Auto never "
            f"assigns the nearest zone: a point outside Michigan or in "
            f"another state's or Canada's water has no Michigan zone. Check "
            f"the coordinate, or choose the zone yourself.{hint}",
            latitude=lat,
            longitude=lon,
        )
    if len(found) > 1:
        names = ", ".join(f"{c.name} ({c.fips})" for c in found)
        raise AutoZoneAmbiguousError(
            f"The point at {_position_text(lat, lon)} lies inside more than "
            f"one county polygon - {names} - in {counties.source}. The county "
            f"data overlaps there, and Auto refuses rather than pick one of "
            f"them: the zone would depend on the order the counties were "
            f"tested in. Choose the zone yourself.",
            latitude=lat,
            longitude=lon,
        )
    county = found[0]

    if system is AutoZoneSystem.SPCS83:
        table: Mapping[str, Zone] = autozone_spcs83.SPCS83_ZONE_BY_FIPS
        zone = table.get(county.fips)
    else:
        zone = autozone_spcs2022.ldp_zone(county.fips, lat)
    if zone is None:
        raise AutoZoneDataError(
            f"{county.name} County ({county.fips}) has no row in the "
            f"{system.value} county table, so no zone can be read for the "
            f"point at {_position_text(lat, lon)}. The county data and the "
            f"table disagree about which counties exist.",
            latitude=lat,
            longitude=lon,
        )
    if zone.system != system.value:
        raise AutoZoneDataError(
            f"The {system.value} table maps {county.name} County to "
            f"{zone}, which is a {zone.system} zone.",
            latitude=lat,
            longitude=lon,
        )
    return ZoneAssignment(zone=zone, county_name=county.name, county_fips=county.fips)


def zones_choosable(system: AutoZoneSystem) -> tuple[Zone, ...]:
    """Every zone ``zone_for`` can return for ``system``, in registry order.

    Read from the same tables ``zone_for`` reads - the SPCS 83 county table,
    and the SPCS2022 table plus the Isle Royale zone its rule adds - so a
    caller that must check something against EVERY zone Auto might choose
    (``job``'s unit gate, work package Z2) asks the rule itself rather than a
    second list that could drift from it. Never includes the statewide
    SPCS2022 zone 260001, which Auto never chooses.
    """
    if not isinstance(system, AutoZoneSystem):
        raise AutoZoneInputError(
            f"zones_choosable needs an AutoZoneSystem (SPCS83 or SPCS2022); "
            f"got {type(system).__name__} ({system!r})."
        )
    if system is AutoZoneSystem.SPCS83:
        used = set(autozone_spcs83.SPCS83_ZONE_BY_FIPS.values())
        registry = SPCS83_ZONES
    else:
        used = set(autozone_spcs2022.LDP_ZONE_BY_FIPS.values()) | {
            autozone_spcs2022.ISLE_ROYALE_ZONE
        }
        registry = SPCS2022_ZONES
    return tuple(zone for zone in registry if zone in used)


def require_tables_cover(counties: CountySet) -> None:
    """Refuse a county set and the zone tables that do not name the same counties.

    Both directions, by FIPS, and the county NAME each table row states must be
    the name the county data gives that FIPS: the statute lists counties by
    name, the data by FIPS, and this is where the two are joined. Called by the
    loader once, so a mismatch fails at load, not at the first point that lands
    in the missing county.
    """
    data = {c.fips: c.name for c in counties.counties}
    for label, names in (
        ("SPCS 83", autozone_spcs83.COUNTY_NAME_BY_FIPS),
        ("SPCS2022", autozone_spcs2022.COUNTY_NAME_BY_FIPS),
    ):
        missing = sorted(set(data) - set(names))
        extra = sorted(set(names) - set(data))
        if missing or extra:
            raise AutoZoneDataError(
                f"The {label} county table and {counties.source} disagree "
                f"about which counties exist: in the data only {missing}, in "
                f"the table only {extra}."
            )
        wrong = sorted(
            f"{fips}: table {names[fips]!r}, data {data[fips]!r}"
            for fips in data
            if names[fips] != data[fips]
        )
        if wrong:
            raise AutoZoneDataError(
                f"The {label} county table names counties differently from "
                f"{counties.source}: {'; '.join(wrong)}."
            )

# PLAN: Options menu, Auto zone, and the observation date in Options

**Status: PROPOSAL, written by the session lead 2026-10-22.** Ships in 0.8.0
together with the WGS 84 build (`docs/PLAN-wgs84.md`). DESIGN.md #71 opens it.
Recon: `review/autozone-r0/RECON.md` (zone boundaries, NCAT as truth) and the
lead's GUI/job map (summarised in §2).

## 1. Scope

### Settled by the owner (2026-10-22)

1. **An Options menu** that switches groups on and off in every system
   dropdown: SPCS 83 zones, SPCS2022 zones, NAD83(2011) geodetic, NATRF2022
   geodetic, and each of the five WGS 84 / ITRF frames. All on by default
   except the five, which are off. **Remembered between runs.**
2. **Auto zone.** An "Auto" entry at the top of the State Plane zone section
   of the list, on both tabs. It picks the zone from each point's
   latitude/longitude, **per point**. On NATRF2022 it picks the **local
   low-distortion zone**, never the statewide one.
3. **The Auto frame is an Options setting** (NAD83(2011) or NATRF2022). A
   lat/long in the other frame is refused for now (no published NAD 83 ⇄
   NATRF2022 transformation, #62); when that bridge exists it converts.
4. **A Multi point file that spans zones writes one CAD (clean PNEZD) file
   per zone.** The audit CSV and the job record name each point's zone.
5. **The observation date leaves both tabs** and moves into Options: "today"
   by default, or a date the user enters. The job record says which.
6. ITRF early-date warning: not added (as built).

### Settled by the session lead, open to the owner's review

- **L1. Auto is an output-side entry only.** A northing/easting does not say
  which zone it is in (the zones overlap in grid space), so Auto is offered
  only as the TO system when the FROM system is geodetic. On the FROM combo it
  is hidden.
- **L2. Auto follows the existing cross-frame rule (#64).** When the Auto
  frame and the input lat/long's frame have no published path, the Auto entry
  is grayed and, if selected, cleared with `FRAME_RESET_STATUS`; `job.run`
  refuses the same pair by name. WGS 84 / ITRF input works with Auto on
  NAD83 (the zone is chosen from the NAD 83 pivot position after HTDP); with
  Auto on NATRF2022 it is refused, as WGS 84 → SPCS2022 already is.
- **L3. The zone is chosen by county, as the law defines it.** Both systems
  are county unions, Great Lakes waters included (MCL 54.231(3)–(5) for
  SPCS 83; NGS's SPCS2022 zones measured as county unions to 0.026 m, with
  Isle Royale split from Keweenaw). MCX bundles **83 water-extended county
  polygons, unsimplified**, plus two tables: county → SPCS 83 zone
  (transcribed from the statute, cited) and county → SPCS2022 LDP zone
  (measured from NGS's beta polygons, `NGS beta` token, REFREEZE-NSRS row),
  and the Isle Royale rule. NGS's own SPCS2022 polygons are land-only and
  would refuse Great Lakes points NCAT accepts, so they are evidence, not
  the bundled data.
- **L4. Point-in-polygon on the job's own geodetic position** (NAD 83(2011)
  for Auto-NAD83, including the HTDP pivot; NATRF2022 for Auto-NATRF). The
  ~1.2 m between the two is inside every boundary band below.
- **L5. A point in no county is refused by name**, never given the nearest
  zone. Outside Michigan, and in Canadian water, is refused.
- **L6.** Superseded by O2.
- **L7. Options are window-level, shared by both tabs.** This reverses
  #26/#43's "tabs share no state" for the Options only; every other control
  stays per tab. Changing any Option clears every displayed Single point
  result (the #26 stale-result rule) and reapplies the dropdown filter.
- **L8. Hiding a group that holds a current selection clears that
  selection** with a status line, exactly as #64's strand rule does. At
  least one geodetic group and one zone group must stay on; the dialog
  refuses an all-off state rather than leaving an empty dropdown.
- **L9. Persistence through `QSettings`** (per user,
  `HKCU\Software\DMARTIN\MCX - Martin Coordinate Exchange`), behind a seam so
  the suite never reads or writes the owner's real registry. A stored value
  MCX does not recognise falls back to the default **and says so** on the
  status line; it never crashes and never guesses.
- **L10. The observation date in Options.** "Today" is the **local** date the
  job runs (Michigan), not the later-of-local-and-UTC used to avoid false
  future refusals. The core keeps refusing a missing date: the GUI now always
  sends one, plus a required `ObservationDateSource` (TODAY or ENTERED) which
  the record prints ("2026-10-22, the date the job ran (Options default)" or
  "…, entered in Options"). A stray source on a job with no WGS 84/ITRF frame
  is refused, as a stray date is. **This reverses PLAN-wgs84 D10's no-default
  rule, on the owner's instruction**, for the "today" choice only; O3.
- **L11. Non-Auto jobs are byte-identical** to the WGS 84 build's output, held
  by the existing digest pins (v0.5.0, pre-W4, W4 disclosure). Every change
  in the outputs is gated on Auto.

### Owner decisions on the lead's questions (2026-10-22)

- **O1. County lines: US Census TIGER 2025** (what NGS built SPCS2022 from,
  and what NCAT uses for it). Measured against the State of Michigan
  Geographic Framework: on land 0.04 m median, 40 m worst; in the lakes
  116 m median, 444 m worst; the North/Central water line up to 11.8 km
  where it meets the international line. NCAT's SPCS 83 land line is 3-17 m
  off TIGER in places; the record names TIGER as the source.
- **O2. Near a zone line: assign only.** A point takes the zone of the
  county it falls in, with no warning and no refusal (MCL 54.234 permits
  either zone where named; the record names each point's zone and county as
  facts). L6 is superseded by this.
- **O3. The observation date.** Options holds a choice: **today** (default)
  or **enter a date**. The choice is remembered; the date is not. With
  "enter a date", the existing date box appears on the main tab, opening
  unanswered ("— choose —") every time MCX starts, and Convert waits for it
  (the WGS 84 build's widget and gating, kept). With "today", no date box is
  shown and the job uses the local date it runs.

## 2. What the recon found that shapes the build

- One function builds all four combos (`controls.zone_combo`); rows can be
  hidden (`setRowHidden`) without rebuilding, so every `findData` and index
  pin stays valid. `direction_for` fails closed on an unknown item type, so
  the Auto item is refused until each consumer handles it.
- The core already converts per point (`project_point(..., target_zone)`,
  `PointConversion.target_zone`), but every output reads
  `settings.target_zone`: `exports.output_stem`, the audit "Target zone"
  cell, `report._job_zones`, the TO block, the "Both zones … exact
  re-projection" sentence, the panel's Zone row, the unit and frame gates.
  With Auto, `target_zone` is None, and each of these crashes, prints a false
  sentence, or **skips a gate silently** (US survey feet on SPCS2022). Every
  one is a work item and a pin.
- `verify_round_trip` checks one clean file against all points; with one file
  per zone it runs per file on that file's points. `_verify_archive` refuses
  an empty member, so a zone with no points gets no file.
- Gate 6 refuses any bundled file byte-identical to one under `review/`, so
  the county file is derived (re-serialised, digest-pinned), never copied.
- NCAT returns the zone for a lat/long in both systems (production REST for
  SPCS 83; the beta web form for SPCS2022). It disagrees with itself near
  the Osceola/Mecosta line because its two systems use different county
  data, so anchors are frozen **outside** the boundary bands only.

## 3. Architecture

- **`michspc/spc/autozone.py`** (core, stdlib): `zone_for(lat, lon, frame)`
  → `ZoneAssignment(zone, county, distance_to_line_m | None)` or
  `AutoZoneRefusal` naming the point. Pure point-in-polygon (even-odd, with a
  documented on-edge rule) over polygons handed in; the county tables are
  core constants with their citations.
- **`michspc/fileio/counties.py`**: the only reader of
  `data/mi_counties_<source>.json` (derived, SHA-256 pinned, geometry
  checks on load as the NGS grids have).
- **`job.py`**: `JobSettings.target_zone` may be `AUTO` (a sentinel object,
  not None) with `auto_frame`; per point the zone is chosen after any HTDP
  pivot, then projected. Unit gate checks the unit against EVERY zone the
  Auto frame can choose; frame gate against the Auto frame.
- **Outputs**: one clean member per zone used, `<stem>_<zone>.csv`; the audit
  CSV's Target zone cell names the point's zone; the record's TO block lists
  each zone used with its point count, the county rule, the data source and
  digest; the audit CSV names each point's county (O2).
- **GUI**: `Options` menu → dialog (toggles, Auto frame, observation date);
  window-level `Options` object read by both tabs; Auto row at the top of
  the zone section; date widgets removed from both tabs.

## 4. Work packages (Opus builders to the lead's brief; lead reviews every diff)

- **Z0** derive the county file and both tables from the recon captures;
  freeze NCAT zone anchors (both systems, outside the bands, including
  Great Lakes, Isle Royale, out-of-state refusals).
- **Z1** `autozone.py` + `counties.py`, pinned to the anchors.
- **Z2** `job.run` Auto: per-point zone, refusals, both gates. **Interim
  Codex gate 1 over Z0–Z2.**
- **Z3** outputs: per-zone clean files, verifiers, audit, record (Auto only;
  every non-Auto digest unchanged).
- **Z4** Options dialog, persistence seam, toggles, Auto entry, the date
  box shown only under "enter a date", both tabs; offscreen previews for the owner.
- **Z5** packaging (spec datas, data pin, LAZY_IMPORTS, gate 6), self-test
  check for Auto, REFREEZE rows, release notes 0.8.0 updated. **Closing
  Codex gate over Z0–Z5**, fixes, narrowing re-confirmation.

Each package: hand-derived expected values, every pin falsified by seeding
(snapshot restore, never `git checkout --`), suite green in `pytest` and
`-O` before commit.

## 5. Still human

- The owner's screen review of both tabs and the Options dialog.
- One real WGS 84 / PPP dataset end to end.
- The clean-profile install proof (METHOD.md §6).
## Non-negotiable conventions (enforce in review)

- Units explicit at every boundary; International feet is the default because
  Michigan legislated it, and the unit in force is stated in every output file.
- Longitude sign convention: **no default in the core** — `JobSettings`
  requires it and `job.run` refuses a geodetic job without it. The GUI dropdown
  opens on positive-west (DESIGN.md #29, owner's instruction); that is a
  decision, not a regression, and #29 says why.
- Fail closed, never fabricate; refusals name the offending item.
- Missing elevation writes `N/A` in factor columns — never `1.0`.
- One authoritative representation per fact; derived values are never stored.
- One entry point per data path; loaders validate as strictly as the UI.
- No uncited constants — document and page, in an adjacent comment.
- Exports never silently clobber; atomic stage-and-rename.
- No load-bearing asserts in production code; the suite runs under `-O`.
- Cross-frame conversion refuses loudly. Never a silent pass-through.
- The rigorous §3.1 Lambert equations are the only computation path. What
  verifies them is external and lives in the suite: the frozen NGS NCAT anchors
  and the published Appendix C constants (DESIGN.md #14).

## Development process

Work packages by subagents → session lead independently re-derives load-bearing
# DESIGN.md — Michigan SPC Zone Converter

**This document is the design authority.** `CLAUDE.md` is a working summary and
may be rewritten freely; this file is *amended*, never rewritten. Decisions are
recorded append-only in the amendment log at the bottom. A superseded decision
stays in the log with a pointer forward — history is evidence, not clutter.

---

## 1. Correctness tier

> **A wrong coordinate here lands on a sealed survey or a recorded legal
> description and moves a boundary.**

Everything below scales from that sentence. When a convenient behavior and a
correct behavior conflict, this sentence is the tiebreaker.

Direct consequences, adopted:

- Independent adversarial review at **both** the interim and closing gates.
- Every expected value in a test is hand-derived in a comment above it, from the
  equation or the published table — never read back from our own output.
- Loaders validate as strictly as the UI. Corrupt input never reaches the core.
- Fail closed. An unhandleable case produces a loud, specific refusal naming the
  offending item. No plausible default is ever fabricated.
- Two independent computation engines run on every point and must agree.

## 2. Scope

**In scope**

- Conversion of coordinate files between the three Michigan SPCS 83 zones:
  MI North 2111, MI Central 2112, MI South 2113 — all Lambert conformal conic.
- Geodetic (latitude/longitude) ⇄ State Plane, either direction.
- Grid scale factor, convergence angle, elevation factor and combined factor
  per point, with geoid separation from a registry of geoid models — GEOID18
  (default) and GEOID12B (#40).
- Vertical datum conversion of elevations, NGVD 29 ⇄ NAVD 88, via NGS
  VERTCON 3.0, with a per-point modeled shift and one-sigma uncertainty and
  the disclosure surfaces of #42 (added across #40–#44; the registry design
  is what NAPGD2022 later arrives through, #22/#32).
- Units: International feet (default and legislated), US survey feet, meters —
  selectable independently for input and output.
- Three outputs per run: a clean PNEZD file, a full-audit CSV, and a plain-text
  job record.

**Deliberately out of scope** (see §10 for the reasons)

UTM; SPCS2022 zones; NAD83 ↔ NATRF2022 transformation; other states; NAD 27;
two-point azimuth/distance computation.

## 3. Primary sources

| Source | Location | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| NOAA Manual NOS NGS 5, *State Plane Coordinate System of 1983*, Stem, Jan 1989, reprinted with minor corrections Mar 1990 | `docs/NOAA_Manual_NOS_NGS_0005.pdf` (committed) | All projection math, zone constants, factor definitions |
| NGS GEOID18 model, grid tile `g2018u3.bin` | `data/` (committed unmodified, SHA-256 pinned) | Geoid separation |
| NGS GEOID12B model, grid tile `g2012bu3.bin` | `data/` (committed unmodified, SHA-256 pinned in its `GeoidModel` record) | Second geoid model in the registry (WP-V5, #40) |
| NGS VERTCON 3.0, release 20190601, `.trn.b` and `.err.b` CONUS grids | `data/` (committed unmodified under NGS's own filenames, SHA-256 pinned) | NGVD 29 ⇄ NAVD 88 shift and its one-sigma uncertainty |
| NOAA TM NOS NGS-84 and `intg.f`; NOAA's published `Vertcon.java` | Read from `ngs.noaa.gov`; findings recorded in #36/#37, harnesses in `review/wp-v4-anchoring/` | The biquadratic scheme and its nearest-node stencil anchoring |
| NGS NCAT service | Frozen fixtures in `tests/fixtures/` | Independent verification anchors, horizontal and vertical |
| NGS geoid height API (`model=14` GEOID18, `model=13` GEOID12B — each response names its own model and the captures refuse a mismatch) | Frozen fixtures in `tests/fixtures/` | Geoid interpolation anchors, both models |
| Prior MATLAB implementation | `docs/reference/SPC_converter_AllZones_Elev.m` | Supplemental only, not authoritative |

Page citations in code comments refer to the **PDF's own page numbering**, not
the printed page numbers (the PDF leads the printed body by 10 pages).

**No uncited constants.** Every empirical coefficient, tolerance or proportion
carries its source document and page in an adjacent comment. Where the source
publishes no number and one is needed, it is declared a *disclosed convention*,
not a citation.

## 4. Data model

The pivot of every conversion is a geodetic position **tagged with its reference
frame**:

```
(zone A, N, E)  --inverse-->  Geodetic{frame, lat, lon}
                --transform-->  Geodetic{frame'}
                --forward-->   (zone B, N, E)
```

Zone-to-zone inside one frame is exact and reversible; the transform step is
currently the identity. Elevation is orthometric height, tagged with its
vertical datum when the job states one. In HORIZONTAL mode it is passed
through unchanged — it does not depend on the horizontal zone. In
HORIZONTAL_AND_VERTICAL mode it is **shifted between the stated vertical
datums before the geoid lookup and the factors** (plan §3.6, #41) — the
"passed through unchanged" sentence this section carried was repealed for
that mode at #41, and every output that carries a shifted height says so
(#42).

Result records produced by the core are frozen. UI layers never mutate them.

## 5. Core computation

**[ANNOTATED at #44: the polynomial engine described below was DELETED at
amendment #14 (owner directive), and this section went uncorrected for three
minor versions — found by the closing gate of the vertical feature. The
rigorous §3.1 equations are the only computation path; what verifies them is
external and lives in the suite: the frozen NGS NCAT anchors and the
published Appendix C constants. CLAUDE.md's conventions section has said so
all along; this body section now matches it.]**

The **rigorous** general Lambert conformal conic mapping equations, manual
§3.1 (pp. 27–29), are the only engine. Valid everywhere; Python's doubles
supply the significant digits the manual warns are needed (§3, p. 25).

~~2. **Polynomial coefficient method** — manual §3.4 (pp. 52–55) with the
Appendix C coefficients (pp. 103–104). Independent cross-check.
Disagreement beyond **0.5 mm** is a named, loud failure.~~ (Deleted, #14:
the polynomials are least-squares fits inside each zone's own latitude band,
so cross-zone conversion — this tool's core use — is extrapolation for them;
measured wrong by metres, #5.)

## 6. Extensibility

**Corrected by amendment #21 (2026-08-06); the original text is quoted there.**
Michigan's published SPCS2022 design is **19 zones on NATRF2022** — a statewide
oblique Mercator plus 18 low-distortion zones, 13 one-parallel Lambert and 5
transverse Mercator. The SPCS 83 North/Central/South zones do not carry forward.
NATRF2022 is finalized in beta but not released, and no official
NAD83(2011)→NATRF2022 transformation exists yet.

The seams below were **claimed** to let that arrive as data rather than a
rewrite. Two independent reviewers attacked that claim at the closing gate and
both returned REWORK-REQUIRED: the protocol, the second constructor and the
transformation seam do not exist in code. Amendment #21 carries the full list,
which is the opening specification of the SPCS2022 work package. They are
retained here as the intended design, not as a description of the code:

- **`Projection` protocol** — `forward(lat, lon)` and `inverse(N, E)`. Lambert
  today; the manual already supplies transverse Mercator (§3.2) and oblique
  Mercator (§3.3) for zone types other states use.
- **Two Lambert constructors** — from two standard parallels (the SPCS 83 form)
  and from a central parallel plus scale factor (the SPCS2022 1SP form).
- **Zone registry as versioned data**, not code. Adding a system means adding
  records and a citation.
- **Frame registry with an explicit transformation seam.**

**Safety rule, non-negotiable:** a conversion whose source and target frames
differ **refuses loudly** until a real transformation is implemented. It must
never pass coordinates through as though NAD 83 and NATRF2022 were the same
thing — that is a silent 1–2 m error on a sealed drawing, which is precisely the
failure the tier sentence exists to prevent.

## 7. Conventions (enforced in review)

- Units are explicit at every boundary. International feet is the default
"""The shipped Michigan county polygons: the only reader of the county file.

``data/mi_counties_tiger2025.json`` holds Michigan's 83 counties as the US
Census Bureau's TIGER/Line 2025 county shapefile draws them - water-extended
into the Great Lakes, unsimplified, every ring and vertex in TIGER's own order,
every coordinate the shapefile's own double (owner's decision O1,
docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md). It is a DERIVED serialization, written by
``review/autozone-z0/derive_counties.py`` from the zip that script
authenticates, and it is what Auto zone tests a position against
(``michspc.spc.autozone``).

**Authenticated on every load, as the NGS grids are** (``geoid.py``): the
whole file is hashed against the digest pinned here before a byte of it is
parsed, then its structure is checked - the format tag, 83 counties, unique
FIPS codes and names, every ring closed and made of finite coordinates inside
Michigan's neighbourhood - and finally its counties are joined against both
zone tables, which must name exactly the same FIPS codes with exactly the same
county names. Each check refuses by name. A county file that fails any of them
is never used: a wrong county polygon assigns a wrong zone with nothing
downstream to notice.

File layout (one JSON object; LF line endings, one county per line, marked
``-text`` in ``.gitattributes`` so a Windows checkout cannot move its digest):

    "format":       "mcx-county-polygons/1"
    "source", "selection", "coordinates", "rings", "derived_by":  provenance text
    "counties":     [{"fips": "26001", "name": "Alcona",
                      "namelsad": "Alcona County",
                      "rings": [[[lon, lat], ...], ...]}, ...]   sorted by FIPS

Longitude negative west, NAD83 geographic, as TIGER stores it.

Packaging (work package Z5): this file must ship under ``data/`` beside the
NGS grids, and this module must be importable in the frozen bundle.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import math
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from michspc.fileio import ngs_grid
from michspc.spc.autozone import (
    AutoZoneDataError,
    County,
    CountySet,
    require_tables_cover,
)

DATA_DIR = ngs_grid.shipped_data_directory()

COUNTIES_FILENAME = "mi_counties_tiger2025.json"
COUNTIES_BYTES = 1_659_316
COUNTIES_SHA256 = "53664dd816375b407c5269cabde565fc89d76e0a3f3ed320fb264240b49f33c3"
"""SHA-256 of the file ``derive_counties.py`` wrote from
tl_2025_us_county.zip (SHA-256
9c6e9d9076abce2670d1de255de3710c35ecca00a7005d88e012dec52d95f763), 2026-10-22."""

COUNTIES_FORMAT = "mcx-county-polygons/1"
COUNTY_COUNT = 83
"""Michigan's counties: MCL 54.231's 15 + 27 + 41."""

COUNTIES_SOURCE = "US Census TIGER/Line 2025 counties"
"""How a refusal and the job record name the county data."""

# Michigan's neighbourhood, generously: TIGER's Michigan counties span about
# 41.70-48.31 N and 90.42-82.12 W (measured from the file). A vertex outside
# this box is not a Michigan county line, whatever else it is.
_LAT_RANGE = (41.0, 49.0)
_LON_RANGE = (-91.0, -82.0)


class CountyDataError(Exception):
    """The shipped county file could not be read, or is not the file pinned."""


def _refuse(path: Path, problem: str) -> CountyDataError:
    return CountyDataError(
        f"The county file {path} cannot be used: {problem}. Auto zone picks a "
        f"zone from these polygons, so a wrong one would assign a wrong zone "
        f"with nothing downstream to notice; it is refused instead. The file "
        f"ships with the program - reinstall if it has been altered."
    )


def _coordinate(value: object) -> float | None:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return None
    number = float(value)
    return number if math.isfinite(number) else None


def _parse_county(path: Path, index: int, record: object) -> County:
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        raise _refuse(path, f"county entry {index} is not an object")
    fips, name, rings = record.get("fips"), record.get("name"), record.get("rings")
    if not (isinstance(fips, str) and len(fips) == 5 and fips.isdigit() and fips.startswith("26")):
        raise _refuse(path, f"county entry {index} has FIPS {fips!r}, not a Michigan (26xxx) code")
    if not (isinstance(name, str) and name.strip() == name and name):
        raise _refuse(path, f"county {fips} has the name {name!r}")
    if not (isinstance(rings, list) and rings):
        raise _refuse(path, f"{name} County ({fips}) has no rings")
    parsed = []
    for r, ring in enumerate(rings):
        if not (isinstance(ring, list) and len(ring) >= 4):
            raise _refuse(
                path, f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} has fewer than 4 vertices"
            )
        vertices = []
        for v, vertex in enumerate(ring):
            if not (isinstance(vertex, list) and len(vertex) == 2):
                raise _refuse(path, f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} vertex {v} is not a [lon, lat] pair")
            lon, lat = _coordinate(vertex[0]), _coordinate(vertex[1])
            if lon is None or lat is None:
                raise _refuse(path, f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} vertex {v} is not two finite numbers: {vertex!r}")
            if not (_LON_RANGE[0] <= lon <= _LON_RANGE[1] and _LAT_RANGE[0] <= lat <= _LAT_RANGE[1]):
                raise _refuse(
                    path,
                    f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} vertex {v} at longitude "
                    f"{lon!r}, latitude {lat!r} is outside Michigan's neighbourhood",
                )
            vertices.append((lon, lat))
        if vertices[0] != vertices[-1]:
            raise _refuse(
                path,
                f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} is not closed: it starts at "
                f"{vertices[0]!r} and ends at {vertices[-1]!r}",
            )
        parsed.append(tuple(vertices))
    return County(fips=fips, name=name, rings=tuple(parsed))


def load_counties(path: Path | None = None, verify_checksum: bool = True) -> CountySet:
    """Read, authenticate and check the county file; return the prepared set.

    ``verify_checksum=False`` exists only so the structural checks can be
    exercised against a deliberately altered copy in the suite. The program
    never passes it.
    """
    path = path or DATA_DIR / COUNTIES_FILENAME
    try:
        raw = path.read_bytes()
    except OSError as error:
        raise CountyDataError(
            f"Could not read the county file at {path}: {error}. This file "
            f"ships with the program; if it is missing the installation is "
            f"incomplete."
        ) from error

    if verify_checksum:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
        if digest != COUNTIES_SHA256:
            raise CountyDataError(
                f"{path} does not match the county file this program was "
                f"built against.\n  expected SHA-256 {COUNTIES_SHA256} "
                f"({COUNTIES_BYTES} bytes)\n  found    SHA-256 {digest} "
                f"({len(raw)} bytes)\nZones chosen from unverified county "
                f"lines could be wrong in ways nothing downstream would "
                f"notice, so it is refused."
            )

    try:
        document = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as error:
        raise _refuse(path, f"it is not valid UTF-8 JSON ({error})") from error
    if not isinstance(document, dict) or document.get("format") != COUNTIES_FORMAT:
        raise _refuse(path, f"its format tag is not {COUNTIES_FORMAT!r}")
    records = document.get("counties")
    if not isinstance(records, list):
        raise _refuse(path, "it has no county list")
    if len(records) != COUNTY_COUNT:
        raise _refuse(path, f"it holds {len(records)} counties, not Michigan's {COUNTY_COUNT}")

    counties = [_parse_county(path, i, record) for i, record in enumerate(records)]
    for field_name in ("fips", "name"):
        values = [getattr(c, field_name) for c in counties]
        repeated = sorted({v for v in values if values.count(v) > 1})
        if repeated:
            raise _refuse(path, f"more than one county has the {field_name} {repeated}")

    try:
        county_set = CountySet(counties, source=COUNTIES_SOURCE)
        require_tables_cover(county_set)
    except AutoZoneDataError as error:
        raise _refuse(path, str(error)) from error
    return county_set


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def default_counties() -> CountySet:
    """The shipped county set, read and authenticated once per process."""
    return load_counties()

+class UndisclosedAutoZoneError(WriteError):
+    """Raised for an Auto zone job, whose outputs cannot yet state what was done.
+
+    The Auto zone build's write guard (docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md, between
+    work packages Z2 and Z3), on the W3 -> W4 precedent of the WGS 84 build
+    (docs/DESIGN.md #70). Z2 lets ``job.run`` choose each point's zone; Z3
+    builds the outputs that can say so - one clean export per zone, the
+    audit CSV's per-point zone and county, the record's TO block listing
+    each zone used, the county rule and its data. Until then every output
+    reads ``settings.target_zone`` as though it were one zone, which on an
+    Auto job is ``AUTO_ZONE``: a stem, a Target zone cell, a zone block and
+    an era sentence would each be missing, false or a crash. So an Auto job
+    converts but is not written. The #41 sequencing rule: disclosure before
+    reachability.
+    """
+
+
+def require_a_disclosed_zone(result: JobResult) -> None:
+    """Refuse to write an Auto zone job until work package Z3 can disclose it.
+
+    Refuses exactly when ``settings.target_zone is AUTO_ZONE`` - decided from
+    the SETTINGS, so an Auto job with no points at all is refused too. Every other job passes untouched and
+    writes byte for byte what it always wrote. Called first by ``write_all``
+    and by ``report.build_report``. Removed by work package Z3.
+    """
+    settings = result.settings
+    if settings.target_zone is not AUTO_ZONE:
+        return
+    frame = getattr(settings.auto_frame, "code", repr(settings.auto_frame))
+    zones = sorted(
+        {point.auto_zone.zone.code for point in result.points if point.auto_zone}
+    )
+    chosen = (
+        f"zones {', '.join(zones)} were chosen for its {len(result.points)} "
+        f"converted point(s)"
+        if zones
+        else "no point was converted"
+    )
+    raise UndisclosedAutoZoneError(
+        f"Nothing was written: this is an Auto zone job (target_zone="
+        f"AUTO_ZONE, zones chosen per point in {frame}); {chosen}. "
+        f"The clean export, the audit CSV and the job record do not yet state "
+        f"each point's own zone and county, or the county rule and data that "
+        f"chose them - they would describe one zone, or none - so an archive "
+        f"of this job would misstate it. That disclosure is the next stage of "
+        f"this development build (docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md, work package "
+        f"Z3); until it exists an Auto job converts but is not written."
+    )

+class AutoZone(Enum):
+    """The Auto zone statement: "choose each point's zone from its position".
+
+    Its one member, ``AUTO_ZONE``, is what ``JobSettings.target_zone`` holds
+    on an Auto job (docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md section 3, work package
+    Z2). It is deliberately NOT None - None already means "this direction
+    has no zone at that end" - and NOT a ``Zone``: no one zone's constants,
+    units or frame describe an Auto job, and a sentinel that duck-typed as a
+    zone would let ``settings.target_zone.frame`` and friends read facts
+    that are false for most of the job's points (the #11-finding-1 lesson).
+    An Enum member, so it is a typed singleton that survives ``copy``,
+    ``deepcopy`` and ``pickle`` as itself, and every test of it is by
+    identity: ``settings.target_zone is AUTO_ZONE``.
+
+    Legal only as the TARGET of a ``GEODETIC_TO_ZONE`` job (plan L1): a
+    northing and easting do not say which zone they are in, so Auto is never
+    an input. It requires ``JobSettings.auto_frame``.
+    """
+
+    AUTO = "auto"
+
+    def __repr__(self) -> str:
+        return "AUTO_ZONE"
+
+
+AUTO_ZONE = AutoZone.AUTO
+"""The Auto zone sentinel. See ``AutoZone``."""
+
+
+AUTO_FRAMES: tuple[tuple[ReferenceFrame, AutoZoneSystem], ...] = (
+    (NAD83_2011, AutoZoneSystem.SPCS83),
+    (NATRF2022, AutoZoneSystem.SPCS2022),
+)
+"""The frames Auto chooses zones in, each with the zone system it chooses
+among (plan section 1 item 3: an Options setting, NAD83(2011) or NATRF2022).
+Checked at import against the zones themselves: every zone Auto can choose
+for a system must be defined on that system's frame, so the pairing is a
+fact the registry confirms, never an assumption."""
+
+
+def _check_auto_frames() -> None:
+    """Refuse to import a frame/system pairing the zones contradict.
+
+    if/raise, never assert: the suite runs under -O.
+    """
+    for frame, system in AUTO_FRAMES:
+        for zone in zones_choosable(system):
+            if zone.frame is not frame:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"AUTO_FRAMES pairs {frame.code} with {system.value}, but "
+                    f"{zone.name} ({zone.code}), a zone Auto can choose in "
+                    f"{system.value}, is defined on {zone.frame.code}."
+                )
+
+
+_check_auto_frames()
+
+
+def auto_zone_system(frame: ReferenceFrame) -> AutoZoneSystem:
+    """The zone system Auto chooses among in ``frame`` (by identity), or a refusal."""
+    for candidate, system in AUTO_FRAMES:
+        if frame is candidate:
+            return system
+    raise ValueError(
+        f"{_frame_label(frame)} is not a frame Auto chooses zones in. Auto "
+        f"chooses among the SPCS 83 zones on {NAD83_2011.code} or the "
+        f"SPCS2022 low-distortion zones on {NATRF2022.code}; pass "
+        f"michspc.spc.frames.NAD83_2011 or michspc.spc.frames.NATRF2022 - "
+        f"the registry's own record, not a copy of it."
+    )
+

+    user typed in Options. Stated beside ``JobSettings.observation_date``
+    exactly when that date is, and refused by name when it is not; the job
+    record prints it (work package Z3).

+    TODAY = "today"
+    ENTERED = "entered"

+class AutoZoneUnplacedPointsError(ValueError):
+    """An Auto job with points no zone could be chosen for: the WHOLE job is refused.
+
+    The house rule (lead's review of work package Z2): every horizontal per-row
+    refusal in this program refuses the job - a latitude or longitude out of
+    range, a position outside HTDP's velocity grid - and Auto follows it. A
+    point in no Michigan county, or claimed by two county polygons, is never
+    given the nearest zone (plan L5) and is never silently dropped from the
+    output; the job converts nothing, and the message names EVERY such point,
+    with the position tested and its frame, so the file can be corrected in
+    one pass. ``points`` carries them as data: ``(point id, latitude,
+    longitude)``, signed decimal degrees, negative west, in ``frame``.
+    """
+

+        frame: ReferenceFrame,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(message)
+        self.points = points
+        self.frame = frame

+def _require_auto_zone_settings(settings: JobSettings) -> None:
+    """The Auto zone statement's own refusals, before anything else reads a zone.
+
+    Work package Z2 (docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md L1, L2). In order:
+
+    * ``AUTO_ZONE`` as ``source_zone`` - never: a northing and easting do not
+      say which zone they are in (the zones overlap in grid coordinates);
+    * ``AUTO_ZONE`` as ``target_zone`` of any direction but
+      ``GEODETIC_TO_ZONE``;
+    * ``AUTO_ZONE`` without ``auto_frame``; ``auto_frame`` without
+      ``AUTO_ZONE`` (the stray-field class, by name);
+    * an ``auto_frame`` that is not a ``ReferenceFrame`` (TypeError), or not
+      the registry's own NAD83(2011) or NATRF2022 record, by identity.
+
+    The pairing of ``auto_frame`` with the input's ``geodetic_frame`` is NOT
+    checked here: it is the frame gate's, through the same
+    ``frames.require_frame_path`` refusal a fixed-zone job meets.
+    """
+    if settings.source_zone is AUTO_ZONE:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "JobSettings.source_zone was AUTO_ZONE. Auto chooses a zone from a "
+            "latitude and longitude, so it can only be the TARGET of a "
+            "geodetic-to-State Plane job: a northing and easting do not say "
+            "which zone they are in - Michigan's zones overlap in grid "
+            "coordinates - so the zone an input is in is never inferred. "
+            "State the zone the coordinates are in."
+        )
+    auto_target = settings.target_zone is AUTO_ZONE
+    if auto_target and settings.direction is not Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"A {settings.direction.name} job was given target_zone=AUTO_ZONE, "
+            f"but Auto zone is the output of a "
+            f"{Direction.GEODETIC_TO_ZONE.name} job only - it chooses each "
+            f"point's zone from that point's latitude and longitude - and "
+            f"this job {_AUTO_TARGET_REASONS[settings.direction]}. State the "
+            f"zone, or None where this direction has no zone."
+        )
+    if settings.auto_frame is None:
+        if auto_target:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"A job with target_zone=AUTO_ZONE needs auto_frame, the frame "
+                f"Auto chooses zones in: {NAD83_2011.code}, whose zones are "
+                f"the three SPCS 83 zones, or {NATRF2022.code}, whose zones "
+                f"are the eighteen SPCS2022 low-distortion zones. It has no "
+                f"default: the two systems put the same point in different "
+                f"zones with different coordinates."
+            )
+        return
+    if not auto_target:
+        zone = settings.target_zone
+        stated = (
+            f"target_zone={zone.name} ({zone.code})"
+            if isinstance(zone, Zone)
+            else "target_zone=None"
+        )
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"A {settings.direction.name} job with {stated} was given "
+            f"auto_frame={_frame_label(settings.auto_frame)}, which only an "
+            f"Auto job (target_zone=AUTO_ZONE) reads. No zone is chosen from "
+            f"a position in this job, so the frame would be one the job "
+            f"record could print and the conversion never used. Pass "
+            f"auto_frame=None."
+        )
+    if not isinstance(settings.auto_frame, ReferenceFrame):
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"JobSettings.auto_frame must be a michspc.spc.frames."
+            f"ReferenceFrame - NAD83_2011 or NATRF2022; got "
+            f"{type(settings.auto_frame).__name__} ({settings.auto_frame!r})."
+        )
+    auto_zone_system(settings.auto_frame)  # refuses any other record

+def today_local() -> datetime.date:
+    """The LOCAL calendar date this job runs - what "today" means as an observation date.

+    Plan L10: an ``ObservationDateSource.TODAY`` date is the date the job ran

"""The shipped Michigan county polygons: the only reader of the county file.

``data/mi_counties_tiger2025.json`` holds Michigan's 83 counties as the US
Census Bureau's TIGER/Line 2025 county shapefile draws them - water-extended
into the Great Lakes, unsimplified, every ring and vertex in TIGER's own order,
every coordinate the shapefile's own double (owner's decision O1,
docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md). It is a DERIVED serialization, written by
``review/autozone-z0/derive_counties.py`` from the zip that script
authenticates, and it is what Auto zone tests a position against
(``michspc.spc.autozone``).

**Authenticated on every load, as the NGS grids are** (``geoid.py``): the
whole file is hashed against the digest pinned here before a byte of it is
parsed, then its structure is checked - the format tag, 83 counties, unique
FIPS codes and names, every ring closed and made of finite coordinates inside
Michigan's neighbourhood - and finally its counties are joined against both
zone tables, which must name exactly the same FIPS codes with exactly the same
county names. Each check refuses by name. A county file that fails any of them
is never used: a wrong county polygon assigns a wrong zone with nothing
downstream to notice.

File layout (one JSON object; LF line endings, one county per line, marked
``-text`` in ``.gitattributes`` so a Windows checkout cannot move its digest):

    "format":       "mcx-county-polygons/1"
    "source", "selection", "coordinates", "rings", "derived_by":  provenance text
    "counties":     [{"fips": "26001", "name": "Alcona",
                      "namelsad": "Alcona County",
                      "rings": [[[lon, lat], ...], ...]}, ...]   sorted by FIPS

Longitude negative west, NAD83 geographic, as TIGER stores it.

Packaging (work package Z5): this file must ship under ``data/`` beside the
NGS grids, and this module must be importable in the frozen bundle.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import math
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from michspc.fileio import ngs_grid
from michspc.spc.autozone import (
    AutoZoneDataError,
    County,
    CountySet,
    require_tables_cover,
)

DATA_DIR = ngs_grid.shipped_data_directory()

COUNTIES_FILENAME = "mi_counties_tiger2025.json"
COUNTIES_BYTES = 1_659_316
COUNTIES_SHA256 = "53664dd816375b407c5269cabde565fc89d76e0a3f3ed320fb264240b49f33c3"
"""SHA-256 of the file ``derive_counties.py`` wrote from
tl_2025_us_county.zip (SHA-256
9c6e9d9076abce2670d1de255de3710c35ecca00a7005d88e012dec52d95f763), 2026-10-22."""

COUNTIES_FORMAT = "mcx-county-polygons/1"
COUNTY_COUNT = 83
"""Michigan's counties: MCL 54.231's 15 + 27 + 41."""

COUNTIES_SOURCE = "US Census TIGER/Line 2025 counties"
"""How a refusal and the job record name the county data."""

# Michigan's neighbourhood, generously: TIGER's Michigan counties span about
# 41.70-48.31 N and 90.42-82.12 W (measured from the file). A vertex outside
# this box is not a Michigan county line, whatever else it is.
_LAT_RANGE = (41.0, 49.0)
_LON_RANGE = (-91.0, -82.0)


class CountyDataError(Exception):
    """The shipped county file could not be read, or is not the file pinned."""


def _refuse(path: Path, problem: str) -> CountyDataError:
    return CountyDataError(
        f"The county file {path} cannot be used: {problem}. Auto zone picks a "
        f"zone from these polygons, so a wrong one would assign a wrong zone "
        f"with nothing downstream to notice; it is refused instead. The file "
        f"ships with the program - reinstall if it has been altered."
    )


def _coordinate(value: object) -> float | None:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return None
    number = float(value)
    return number if math.isfinite(number) else None


def _parse_county(path: Path, index: int, record: object) -> County:
    if not isinstance(record, dict):
        raise _refuse(path, f"county entry {index} is not an object")
    fips, name, rings = record.get("fips"), record.get("name"), record.get("rings")
    if not (isinstance(fips, str) and len(fips) == 5 and fips.isdigit() and fips.startswith("26")):
        raise _refuse(path, f"county entry {index} has FIPS {fips!r}, not a Michigan (26xxx) code")
    if not (isinstance(name, str) and name.strip() == name and name):
        raise _refuse(path, f"county {fips} has the name {name!r}")
    if not (isinstance(rings, list) and rings):
        raise _refuse(path, f"{name} County ({fips}) has no rings")
    parsed = []
    for r, ring in enumerate(rings):
        if not (isinstance(ring, list) and len(ring) >= 4):
            raise _refuse(
                path, f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} has fewer than 4 vertices"
            )
        vertices = []
        for v, vertex in enumerate(ring):
            if not (isinstance(vertex, list) and len(vertex) == 2):
                raise _refuse(path, f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} vertex {v} is not a [lon, lat] pair")
            lon, lat = _coordinate(vertex[0]), _coordinate(vertex[1])
            if lon is None or lat is None:
                raise _refuse(path, f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} vertex {v} is not two finite numbers: {vertex!r}")
            if not (_LON_RANGE[0] <= lon <= _LON_RANGE[1] and _LAT_RANGE[0] <= lat <= _LAT_RANGE[1]):
                raise _refuse(
                    path,
                    f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} vertex {v} at longitude "
                    f"{lon!r}, latitude {lat!r} is outside Michigan's neighbourhood",
                )
            vertices.append((lon, lat))
        if vertices[0] != vertices[-1]:
            raise _refuse(
                path,
                f"{name} County ({fips}) ring {r} is not closed: it starts at "
                f"{vertices[0]!r} and ends at {vertices[-1]!r}",
            )
        parsed.append(tuple(vertices))
    return County(fips=fips, name=name, rings=tuple(parsed))


def load_counties(path: Path | None = None, verify_checksum: bool = True) -> CountySet:
    """Read, authenticate and check the county file; return the prepared set.

    ``verify_checksum=False`` exists only so the structural checks can be
    exercised against a deliberately altered copy in the suite. The program
    never passes it.
    """
    path = path or DATA_DIR / COUNTIES_FILENAME
    try:
        raw = path.read_bytes()
    except OSError as error:
        raise CountyDataError(
            f"Could not read the county file at {path}: {error}. This file "
            f"ships with the program; if it is missing the installation is "
            f"incomplete."
        ) from error

    if verify_checksum:
        digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
        if digest != COUNTIES_SHA256:
            raise CountyDataError(
                f"{path} does not match the county file this program was "
                f"built against.\n  expected SHA-256 {COUNTIES_SHA256} "
                f"({COUNTIES_BYTES} bytes)\n  found    SHA-256 {digest} "
                f"({len(raw)} bytes)\nZones chosen from unverified county "
                f"lines could be wrong in ways nothing downstream would "
                f"notice, so it is refused."
            )

    try:
        document = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as error:
        raise _refuse(path, f"it is not valid UTF-8 JSON ({error})") from error
    if not isinstance(document, dict) or document.get("format") != COUNTIES_FORMAT:
        raise _refuse(path, f"its format tag is not {COUNTIES_FORMAT!r}")
    records = document.get("counties")
    if not isinstance(records, list):
        raise _refuse(path, "it has no county list")
    if len(records) != COUNTY_COUNT:
        raise _refuse(path, f"it holds {len(records)} counties, not Michigan's {COUNTY_COUNT}")

    counties = [_parse_county(path, i, record) for i, record in enumerate(records)]
    for field_name in ("fips", "name"):
        values = [getattr(c, field_name) for c in counties]
        repeated = sorted({v for v in values if values.count(v) > 1})
        if repeated:
            raise _refuse(path, f"more than one county has the {field_name} {repeated}")

    try:
        county_set = CountySet(counties, source=COUNTIES_SOURCE)
        require_tables_cover(county_set)
    except AutoZoneDataError as error:
        raise _refuse(path, str(error)) from error
    return county_set


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def default_counties() -> CountySet:
    """The shipped county set, read and authenticated once per process."""
    return load_counties()

+class UndisclosedAutoZoneError(WriteError):
+    """Raised for an Auto zone job, whose outputs cannot yet state what was done.
+
+    The Auto zone build's write guard (docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md, between
+    work packages Z2 and Z3), on the W3 -> W4 precedent of the WGS 84 build
+    (docs/DESIGN.md #70). Z2 lets ``job.run`` choose each point's zone; Z3
+    builds the outputs that can say so - one clean export per zone, the
+    audit CSV's per-point zone and county, the record's TO block listing
+    each zone used, the county rule and its data. Until then every output
+    reads ``settings.target_zone`` as though it were one zone, which on an
+    Auto job is ``AUTO_ZONE``: a stem, a Target zone cell, a zone block and
+    an era sentence would each be missing, false or a crash. So an Auto job
+    converts but is not written. The #41 sequencing rule: disclosure before
+    reachability.
+    """
+
+
+def require_a_disclosed_zone(result: JobResult) -> None:
+    """Refuse to write an Auto zone job until work package Z3 can disclose it.
+
+    Refuses exactly when ``settings.target_zone is AUTO_ZONE`` - decided from
+    the SETTINGS, so an Auto job with no points at all is refused too. Every other job passes untouched and
+    writes byte for byte what it always wrote. Called first by ``write_all``
+    and by ``report.build_report``. Removed by work package Z3.
+    """
+    settings = result.settings
+    if settings.target_zone is not AUTO_ZONE:
+        return
+    frame = getattr(settings.auto_frame, "code", repr(settings.auto_frame))
+    zones = sorted(
+        {point.auto_zone.zone.code for point in result.points if point.auto_zone}
+    )
+    chosen = (
+        f"zones {', '.join(zones)} were chosen for its {len(result.points)} "
+        f"converted point(s)"
+        if zones
+        else "no point was converted"
+    )
+    raise UndisclosedAutoZoneError(
+        f"Nothing was written: this is an Auto zone job (target_zone="
+        f"AUTO_ZONE, zones chosen per point in {frame}); {chosen}. "
+        f"The clean export, the audit CSV and the job record do not yet state "
+        f"each point's own zone and county, or the county rule and data that "
+        f"chose them - they would describe one zone, or none - so an archive "
+        f"of this job would misstate it. That disclosure is the next stage of "
+        f"this development build (docs/PLAN-options-autozone.md, work package "
+        f"Z3); until it exists an Auto job converts but is not written."
+    )

"""One conversion job, end to end.

Reads a coordinate file, converts every point, and produces the three outputs
the owner specified: a clean PNEZD export for CAD, a full-audit CSV, and a
plain-text job record explaining both.

This module is the only place that knows about all three layers at once. The
computation core knows nothing of files; the file layer knows nothing of zones;
this joins them and owns the unit conversion at the boundary.

Nothing here writes anything. ``run`` produces an immutable ``JobResult``; the
caller decides whether and where to commit it to disk. That keeps the whole
pipeline testable without a filesystem, and keeps the GUI's "preview then
convert" behaviour honest - what is previewed is what is written.
"""
