 succeeded in 312ms:
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    source_frame: ReferenceFrame,
    target_zone: Zone,
    context: str = "point",
    *,
    epoch: htdp.ObservationEpoch | None = None,
    height: TransformHeight | None = None,
) -> PointConversion:
    """Convert a geodetic position into a zone's grid coordinates.

    The geodetic-input case. No inverse step is performed, so the source zone is
    the target zone.

    ``source_frame`` is the reference frame the latitude and longitude are
    expressed in, and it is **required with no default**. A latitude and
    longitude alone do not say which frame they belong to, and NAD 83 and
    NATRF2022 differ by one to two metres over North America; projecting a
    NATRF2022 position with the SPCS 83 constants yields a coordinate that looks
    entirely ordinary and is wrong by more than the width of a road. The
    equivalent zone-to-zone refusal has existed since the beginning
    (``convert_point``); this closes the geodetic-input door on the same rule.
    See docs/DESIGN.md sections 4 and 6, and amendment #11 finding 1.

    Refuses with ``FrameMismatchError`` if no registered path joins the
    position's frame to the target zone's frame.

    **A WGS 84 or ITRF position is transformed first** (plan W3): when the
    registered path is HTDP's - one of the five time-dependent frames into an
    SPCS 83 zone - the position goes to NAD83(2011) at 2010.0 by
    ``htdp.to_nad83`` and that pivot is projected. ``epoch`` (the date the
    position was observed) and ``height`` (what HTDP is handed, and its
    convention) are then REQUIRED, keyword-only, and refused on a same-frame
    projection. The result's ``latitude`` and ``longitude`` are the NAD 83
    pivot; the position as given is ``external_position``.
    """
    if not isinstance(source_frame, ReferenceFrame):
        raise TypeError(
            f"project_point needs the reference frame the geodetic position is "
            f"expressed in, as its third argument; got "
            f"{type(source_frame).__name__} ({source_frame!r}). A latitude and "
            f"longitude do not carry their own frame, and the frame decides "
            f"whether the resulting State Plane coordinate is right or is one "
            f"to two metres out. Pass michspc.spc.frames.NAD83_2011 for an "
            f"NAD 83 position."
        )

    target_zone = _require_zone(target_zone, "target zone", "project_point")

    # The site a WGS 84 or ITRF position reaches first - WGS84(G2296) into an
    # SPCS 83 zone is a REGISTERED path - and projecting its latitude and
    # longitude unchanged would put a WGS 84 position on the NAD 83 grid,
    # about 1.3 m out in Michigan. So the path is applied, once, before the
    # projection: the pivot projected is always in the zone's own frame.
    path = require_an_applicable_path(
        require_frame_path(source_frame, target_zone.frame)
    )
    _require_transform_arguments(path, epoch, height, "project_point")
    pivot_latitude, pivot_longitude, evidence = _apply_frame_path(
        path, latitude, longitude, epoch, height
    )

    (
        northing,
        easting,
        convergence,
        scale,
        warnings,
    ) = from_geodetic(pivot_latitude, pivot_longitude, target_zone, context)

    return PointConversion(
        source_zone=target_zone,
        target_zone=target_zone,
        # The registry's own record, which the frame gate has just required
        # the caller's to equal (frames._canonical): every reader downstream
        # reads the facts the gate checked, never a caller's copy of them.
        # The TARGET end, because the pivot is in the zone's frame - on an
        # identity the two ends are one record, so a same-frame projection
        # carries exactly the record it always did.
        frame=path.target,
        source_northing=northing,
        source_easting=easting,
        latitude=pivot_latitude,
        longitude=pivot_longitude,
        target_northing=northing,
        target_easting=easting,
        source_convergence=convergence,
        source_scale_factor=scale,
        target_convergence=convergence,
        target_scale_factor=scale,
        warnings=warnings,
        **evidence,
    )


def pivot_path(source_frame: ReferenceFrame) -> FrameTransformation:
    """The path from a geodetic position's own frame to the frame of its pivot.

    For the vertical-only job on geodetic input (plan decision D8), which
    converts no position and yet needs one: every grid it reads - the geoid
    models, VERTCON - is published against NAD 83. So:

    * a plate-fixed frame's pivot is the position itself - its IDENTITY
      record, which also refuses a frame the registry does not carry;
    * a time-dependent frame's pivot is the position carried to NAD83(2011)
      by its registered HTDP path. The registry deliberately holds NO
      identity for these frames (plan W2), and none is added: a position
      left in WGS 84 and looked up in a NAD 83 grid is the error this exists
      to prevent;
    * the bare WGS 84 label is refused by name, by ``require_frame_path``.

    Asked of the REGISTRY's record (``resolve_frame``), never of the caller's,
    so a disagreeing copy is refused before its epoch kind is read (interim
    gate 1, finding L4). One statement, read by ``geodetic_position`` and by
    ``job.run``'s settings gate, so the two gates on this direction (interim
    gate 1, finding L5) cannot choose different paths.
    """
    frame = resolve_frame(source_frame)
    if frame.is_time_dependent:
        return require_an_applicable_path(require_frame_path(frame, NAD83_2011))
    return require_an_applicable_path(require_frame_path(frame, frame))


def geodetic_position(
    latitude: float,
    longitude: float,
    source_frame: ReferenceFrame,
    context: str = "point",
    *,
    epoch: htdp.ObservationEpoch | None = None,
    height: TransformHeight | None = None,
) -> PointConversion:
    """A geodetic position with no zone on either end.

    Exists for the vertical-only job whose input is geodetic
    (``michspc.job``, ``Direction.VERTICAL_ONLY`` with ``source_zone=None``):
    the vertical shift and the geoid lookup need the pivot latitude and
    longitude, and nothing in that job involves a State Plane zone. Every
    zone-derived field is None - never a fabricated zone, whose scale factor
    and convergence would be plausible numbers describing a projection nobody
    chose. ``factors_at`` accepts the None scale factor and reports the grid
    scale and combined factors as absent while still computing the elevation
    factor, which needs no zone.

    ``source_frame`` is required with no default, exactly as
    ``project_point`` requires it and for the same reason: a latitude and
    longitude alone do not say which frame they belong to, and the NGS grids
    this position is looked up in are published against NAD 83. No projection
    runs here, so no extent warning can be raised - there is no zone to have
    an extent.

    **Its own frame gate** (interim gate 1 of the WGS 84 build, finding L5).
    This function used to ask no frame question at all, so a vertical-only job
    had one gate, at its settings, where every other direction has two: with
    the settings branch removed, a WGS84(G2296) ellipsoid-height job wrote
    NAVD 88 198.085 m, its WGS 84 h taken as NAD 83's - about 1.07 m low. Now
    the position goes through ``pivot_path``: a plate-fixed frame's identity,
    or a time-dependent frame's HTDP path to NAD83(2011) (plan D8), with the
    bare WGS 84 label and every unregistered frame refused by name. On that
    path the pivot (``latitude``, ``longitude``) is the NAD 83 position the
    grids are read at, and ``external_position`` is the input exactly as
    given; ``epoch`` and ``height`` are required there and refused elsewhere.
    """
    if not isinstance(source_frame, ReferenceFrame):
        raise TypeError(
            f"geodetic_position needs the reference frame the position is "
            f"expressed in, as its third argument; got "
            f"{type(source_frame).__name__} ({source_frame!r}). A latitude "
            f"and longitude do not carry their own frame. Pass "
            f"michspc.spc.frames.NAD83_2011 for an NAD 83 position."
        )
    # pivot_path resolves the record first, so a record that names a
    # registered frame must BE that frame's record (interim gate 1, finding
    # L4) before anything reads its epoch kind - and the result carries the
    # registry's record, never the caller's.
    path = pivot_path(source_frame)
    _require_transform_arguments(path, epoch, height, "geodetic_position")
    pivot_latitude, pivot_longitude, evidence = _apply_frame_path(
        path, latitude, longitude, epoch, height
    )

    return PointConversion(
        source_zone=None,
        target_zone=None,
        # The pivot's frame: the identity's one record, or NAD83(2011) at the
        # end of the HTDP path.
        frame=path.target,
        source_northing=None,
        source_easting=None,
        latitude=pivot_latitude,
    """
    if frame_path is None or frame_path.is_identity:
        return None
    if elevation_m is None:
        return TransformHeight(HeightConvention.NOT_RECORDED, None)
    if settings.input_height_kind is HeightKind.ELLIPSOID:
        return TransformHeight(HeightConvention.ELLIPSOID, elevation_m)
    return TransformHeight(HeightConvention.ORTHOMETRIC, elevation_m)


def written_geodetic_position(conversion: PointConversion) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """The latitude and longitude a job with a geodetic OUTPUT writes, signed.

    The position in the frame the path ENDS in: the WGS 84 or ITRF position
    when the path carries the pivot out to one (``external_position``), the
    NAD 83 pivot otherwise - including every same-frame job, whose columns are
    the pivot exactly as before. Writing the pivot under a WGS 84 job's label
    is the silent pass-through the W2 guard existed to stop.

    Public since work package W4, because it is also the position the
    geodetic exports STATE: ``exports`` builds the DMS sibling from it and
    every verifier checks the written files against it, so the file layer and
    the conversion cannot come to mean different positions by "the target"
    (docs/PLAN-wgs84.md section 3.6, the verifier hazard).
    """
    path = conversion.frame_transformation
    if path is not None and path.target.is_time_dependent:
        external = conversion.external_position
        return external.latitude, external.longitude
    return conversion.latitude, conversion.longitude


def _unconverted_ellipsoid_z_sentence(conversion: PointConversion) -> str:
    """What a horizontal job's Z holds when no geoid separation could be read."""
    if conversion.is_transformed:
        return (
            f"The Z column carries the ellipsoid height transformed with the "
            f"position into {conversion.frame_transformation.target.code}, not "
            f"converted to an elevation, and the elevation and combined "
            f"factors read "
        )
    return (
        "The Z column carries the ellipsoid height as supplied, unconverted, "
        "and the elevation and combined factors read "
    )


def _point_named_htdp_refusal(
    error: htdp.HtdpRefusal,
    context: str,
    settings: JobSettings,
    frame_path: FrameTransformation | None,
    geodetic_input: bool,
) -> htdp.HtdpRefusal:
    """An HTDP refusal raised for one row, restated for that row.

    Interim gate 2 of the WGS 84 build, finding L4: through ``job.run`` the
    velocity-window refusal named no point - one bad row refused a whole
    file with nothing to find it by - and on a path out of NAD 83 it labelled
    the NAD83(2011) pivot with the target frame and advised checking a
    longitude sign the file never held. The frame is now the position's own
    (the path's SOURCE end, the position ``convert`` hands HTDP in either
    direction), the point is named, and the advice is the one that applies
    to where the position came from: the file's longitude convention on a
    geodetic input, the zone and unit on a grid input.

    **The type is kept**: a ``HtdpVelocityGridError`` comes back as one, and
    every other ``HtdpRefusal`` as its own class, with this row's context
    prefixed. Chosen over wrapping in ``ValueError`` (which the per-row
    refusals around it raise) because every caller that already catches the
    HTDP family - by ``HtdpRefusal`` or by the subclass - keeps catching it,
    and a refusal of the TRANSFORMATION stays distinguishable from a refusal
    of the file's contents. The cost, recorded for W5: ``HtdpRefusal``
    subclasses neither ``ValueError`` nor ``FrameMismatchError``, so the GUI
    must catch it explicitly. Both tabs catch ``Exception`` around
    ``job.run`` today and show its message in full, so nothing escapes; W5
    must keep it that way.
    """
    if (
        not isinstance(error, htdp.HtdpVelocityGridError)
        or error.reason is None
        or frame_path is None
        or frame_path.is_identity
        or error.position_frame != frame_path.source.htdp_frame.name
    ):
        # The defect-only node refusal, any other HTDP refusal, or a
        # position whose frame is not the one this function would name:
        # HTDP's own words, which name their own frame, with the point.
        return type(error)(f"{context}: {error}")
    frame = frame_path.source
    # Worded for BOTH tabs (closing gate of the WGS 84 build, finding L3).
    # The Single point tab reaches this refusal with a typed point, so the
    # sentences name no file. And on its DMS entry the hemisphere letter, not
    # the longitude convention, decides the sign, so the advice does not
    # presume the convention decided it: it asks for the signs to be checked
    # - the refused position above is printed signed, so a wrong one is
    # visible - and states the job's convention as the fact it is (the DMS
    # page composes its text in that convention too, ``fileio.dms``). Chosen
    # over telling the core how the point was typed: no computation reads the
    # entry form, and a settings field nothing computes from is the
    # stray-field class this module refuses elsewhere.
    if geodetic_input:
        origin = "the supplied position"
        advice = (
            f"Check that the point is in Michigan, and that its latitude and "
            f"longitude carry the right signs: this job reads longitudes "
            f"written {settings.longitude_convention.value}, and a latitude "
            f"or longitude whose sign is the wrong way round lands on the "
            f"other side of the world."
        )
    else:
        origin = (
            f"the position the {settings.source_zone.name} northing and "
            f"easting give"
        )
        advice = (
            f"Check that the point is in Michigan, and that the northing and "
            f"easting are {settings.source_zone.name} coordinates in "
            f"{settings.input_unit.code}."
        )
    return htdp.HtdpVelocityGridError(
        f"{context}: cannot transform {origin} - latitude "
        f"{error.latitude:.6f}, longitude {error.longitude:.6f} (signed, "
        f"negative west), in {frame.code} - to {frame_path.target.code}: "
        f"{error.reason} {advice}",
        latitude=error.latitude,
        longitude=error.longitude,
        position_frame=error.position_frame,
        reason=error.reason,
    )

        return source, target

    if settings.direction is not Direction.ZONE_TO_ZONE:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The single-point display has no layout for a "
            f"{settings.direction.name} job. Refused rather than drawing it as "
            f"zone to zone, which would show coordinates from zones the job "
            f"never had."
        )

    # Zone to zone. The geodetic pivot the conversion passed through is a real
    # computed result and independent of neither end, so it is shown - under
    # OUTPUT, with the target zone's factors.
    source = ResultSection(
        INPUT_TITLE,
        (
            *_grid_values(
                settings.source_zone,
                settings.input_unit,
                point.row.northing,
                point.row.easting,
                point.row.elevation,
                elevation_label=input_elevation_label,
            ),
            ResultValue(
                GRID_FACTOR_LABEL, fmt.factor(conversion.source_scale_factor)
            ),
            ResultValue(
                CONVERGENCE_LABEL,
                fmt.convergence_display(conversion.source_convergence),
            ),
        ),
    )
    target = ResultSection(
        OUTPUT_TITLE,
        (
            *_grid_values(
                settings.target_zone,
                settings.output_unit,
                point.output_northing,
                point.output_easting,
                point.output_elevation,
                elevation_label=output_elevation_label,
            ),
            *vertical_rows,
            *_geodetic_values(conversion, positive_west),
            ResultValue(GRID_FACTOR_LABEL, fmt.factor(factors.grid_scale_factor)),
            ResultValue(
                CONVERGENCE_LABEL,
                fmt.convergence_display(conversion.target_convergence),
            ),
            *_elevation_dependent_values(factors, ellipsoid_input, pivot_code),
        ),
    )
    return source, target


def single_point_warnings(result: JobResult) -> str:
    """Every warning the single converted point raised, or ``NO_WARNINGS``.

    Separate from ``single_point_sections`` because the owner put warnings in a
    field of their own (docs/DESIGN.md amendment #30) - but built from the same
            f"states method {self.method!r}, which has no direction "
            f"statement. Add one written from the record's fields."
        )

    def _htdp_direction_statement(self) -> str:
        """HTDP's direction-specific composition, from the frames' own records.

        HTDP evaluates the Helmert at the INPUT epoch and then propagates the
        position with the OUTPUT frame's velocity (``htdp.f:3229-3273``;
        review/wgs84-w0/RECON.md section 1.4) - so the two directions are not
        mirror images, and each sentence says which it is.
        """
        source, target = self.source, self.target
        if source.is_time_dependent:
            source_epoch = "at the observation epoch"
            target_epoch = f"at its reference epoch {target.reference_epoch!r}"
            helmert_at = "the observation epoch"
            span = f"from the observation epoch to {target.reference_epoch!r}"
        else:
            source_epoch = f"at its reference epoch {source.reference_epoch!r}"
            target_epoch = "at the observation epoch"
            helmert_at = f"{source.reference_epoch!r}"
            span = f"from {source.reference_epoch!r} to the observation epoch"
        if target.is_time_dependent:
            velocity = (
                f"the {target.code} velocity, which includes the full motion "
                f"of the North American plate"
            )
        else:
            velocity = (
                f"the {target.code} velocity, which is the small intraplate "
                f"motion left in a plate-fixed frame"
            )
        return (
            f"The position is transformed from {source.name} ({source.code}) "
            f"{source_epoch} to {target.name} ({target.code}) {target_epoch} "
            f"by {_HTDP_SOURCE}. HTDP evaluates the 14-parameter Helmert "
            f"transformation at the input epoch, {helmert_at}, and then "
            f"propagates the position {span} with the output frame's velocity: "
            f"{velocity}, from HTDP's ITRF2008 velocity grid for its region 6, "
            f"interpolated bilinearly. When the observation date is "
            f"{htdp.NAD83_2011_EPOCH.date.isoformat()} the span is zero and "
            f"HTDP applies the Helmert transformation alone."
        )

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.source.code} -> {self.target.code}"


_IDENTITY_NAD83_2011 = FrameTransformation(
    source=NAD83_2011,
    target=NAD83_2011,
    citation=_IDENTITY_CITATION,
)

_IDENTITY_NATRF2022 = FrameTransformation(
    source=NATRF2022,
    target=NATRF2022,
    citation=_IDENTITY_CITATION,
)

# There is deliberately NO identity for WGS84. An unusable frame gets no
# registered path of any kind, so that removing the usability check could never
# leave a WGS 84 job quietly running as an identity - it would still have to
# get past a missing registry entry. Pinned.
#
# And deliberately NO identity for the five time-dependent frames either
# (plan W2). Every grid this program reads a position against - GEOID18,
# GEOID12B, VERTCON 3.0 - is published against NAD 83, so even a job that
# leaves a WGS 84 position in its own frame needs it carried to NAD83(2011)
# first. Work package W3 decided how such a job runs (plan D8): the
# vertical-only job's pivot is found through the frame's registered path to
# NAD83(2011) (``convert.pivot_path``), never through an identity - so an
# identity here could only ever be the WGS 84 position looked up in a NAD 83
# grid. Pinned.


def _htdp_citation(source: ReferenceFrame, target: ReferenceFrame) -> str:
    other = target if source.code == NAD83_2011.code else source
    return (
        f"{_HTDP_SOURCE}, transcribed by michspc.spc.htdp: TRFPOS "
        f"(htdp.f:3175-3294) between {NAD83_2011.code} at epoch "
        f"{NAD83_2011.reference_epoch!r} (docs/PLAN-wgs84.md decision D1) and "
        f"{other.code}. Reproduced to HTDP's printed digit on every frozen "
        f"anchor in tests/fixtures/htdp_anchors.py (review/wgs84-w0/)"
    )


def _htdp_pair(
    source: ReferenceFrame, target: ReferenceFrame
) -> FrameTransformation:
    return FrameTransformation(
        source=source,
        target=target,
        citation=_htdp_citation(source, target),
        method=FrameTransformationMethod.HTDP_V3_6_0,
    )


_HTDP_TRANSFORMATIONS: tuple[FrameTransformation, ...] = tuple(
    record
    for frame in _TIME_DEPENDENT_OFFERED
    for record in (_htdp_pair(frame, NAD83_2011), _htdp_pair(NAD83_2011, frame))
)
"""Ten records: each time-dependent frame to NAD83(2011), and back."""


FRAME_TRANSFORMATIONS: Mapping[
    tuple[ReferenceFrame, ReferenceFrame], FrameTransformation
] = MappingProxyType(
    {
        (NAD83_2011, NAD83_2011): _IDENTITY_NAD83_2011,
        (NATRF2022, NATRF2022): _IDENTITY_NATRF2022,
        **{
            (record.source, record.target): record
            for record in _HTDP_TRANSFORMATIONS
        },
    }
)

"""Re-capture NGS's SPCS2022 zone polygons for Michigan (re-freeze harness).

    py -I review/autozone-z0/capture_ngs_polygons.py OUTPUT.json

Fetches the 18 Michigan features of NGS's "Beta SPCS2022 Multizone Complete
Zones Feature Layer View" (ArcGIS item 3e6a8ce23a814b62ae38993394669d8e) in
NAD83 geographic (outSR 4269), the query the autozone-r0 recon used for
review/autozone-r0/raw/ngs_fs/mi_4269.json (RECON.md section 2.1), writes the
response unmodified to OUTPUT, and prints its SHA-256 beside the frozen
capture's. A matching digest means NGS's polygons have not moved; any other
digest means re-running tests/test_autozone_tables.py against the new capture
and the full re-freeze cycle of docs/REFREEZE-NSRS.md. Never writes over the
frozen capture itself. Stdlib only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import sys
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

SERVICE = (
    "https://services2.arcgis.com/C8EMgrsFcRFL6LrL/arcgis/rest/services/"
    "Alpha_SPCS2022_Multizone_Complete_Zones_Feature_Layer_View/FeatureServer/0/query"
)
FROZEN = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "autozone-r0" / "raw" / "ngs_fs" / "mi_4269.json"
FROZEN_SHA256 = "658c4ead203c9ed2a727a29aee8d88ecc834a750cb1c135a83ef710c7d3f2099"
UA = "MCX-autozone-refreeze/0.1 (owner: martin71337; survey software verification)"


def main() -> None:
    out = Path(sys.argv[1])
    if out.resolve() == FROZEN.resolve():
        raise SystemExit("refusing to overwrite the frozen capture")
    query = urllib.parse.urlencode(
        {"where": "StateAbrv='MI'", "outFields": "ZoneCode,AbrvFull", "outSR": "4269",
         "returnGeometry": "true", "geometryPrecision": "10", "orderByFields": "ZoneCode",
         "f": "json"}
    )
    request = urllib.request.Request(SERVICE + "?" + query, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=300) as response:
        body = response.read()
    out.write_bytes(body)
    digest = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
    print(f"fetched {len(body)} bytes, SHA-256 {digest}")
    print(f"frozen  SHA-256 {FROZEN_SHA256} -> {'UNCHANGED' if digest == FROZEN_SHA256 else 'DIFFERENT'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""autozone-r0: load every captured boundary source into one metric frame.

Recon only. Reads the raw captures under raw/ (untrusted downloads, read as
data) and returns shapely geometries in EPSG:3078 (NAD83 / Michigan Oblique
Mercator, metres) so offsets between sources can be measured in metres.

Run with the scratch venv:  <venv>/python -I load_sources.py

LL_TO_M = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:4269", "EPSG:3078", always_xy=True)
M_TO_LL = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:3078", "EPSG:4269", always_xy=True)


def norm(name: str) -> str:
    n = name.strip().replace("Saint ", "St. ")
    return n


def esri_rings_to_geom(rings):
    """Esri JSON rings -> shapely (outer rings clockwise, holes ccw)."""
    shells, holes = [], []
    for r in rings:
        if len(r) < 4:
            continue
        a = 0.0
        for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in zip(r, r[1:]):
            a += (x2 - x1) * (y2 + y1)
        (shells if a > 0 else holes).append(Polygon(r))
    polys = []
    for s in shells:
        hs = [h for h in holes if s.contains(h.representative_point())]
        p = s
        for h in hs:
            p = p.difference(h)
        polys.append(p)
    return unary_union(polys)


def web_mercator_to_ll(x, y, z=None):
    R = 6378137.0
    lon = math.degrees(x / R)
    lat = math.degrees(2.0 * math.atan(math.exp(y / R)) - math.pi / 2.0)
    return lon, lat


def ll_to_m(g):
    return transform(lambda x, y, z=None: LL_TO_M.transform(x, y), g)


def counties_mgf():
    """State of Michigan 'County Boundaries-Extended' (MGF), EPSG:3078."""
    p = os.path.join(RAW, "mi_counties_extended", "counties_native.json")
    d = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    out = {}
    for f in d["features"]:
        out[norm(f["attributes"]["Name"])] = esri_rings_to_geom(
            f["geometry"]["rings"])
    return out, d


def counties_tiger():
    """Census TIGER/Line 2025 counties, STATEFP 26, NAD83 -> EPSG:3078."""
    p = os.path.join(RAW, "tiger", "tl_2025_us_county.zip")
    z = zipfile.ZipFile(p)
    shp = io.BytesIO(z.read("tl_2025_us_county.shp"))
    dbf = io.BytesIO(z.read("tl_2025_us_county.dbf"))
    shx = io.BytesIO(z.read("tl_2025_us_county.shx"))
    r = shapefile.Reader(shp=shp, dbf=dbf, shx=shx, encoding="latin-1")
    fields = [f[0] for f in r.fields[1:]]
    out, attrs = {}, {}
    for sr in r.iterShapeRecords():
        rec = dict(zip(fields, sr.record))
        if rec["STATEFP"] != "26":
            continue
        g = shape(sr.shape.__geo_interface__)
        out[norm(rec["NAME"])] = ll_to_m(g)
        attrs[norm(rec["NAME"])] = rec
    return out, attrs


def ngs_ldp():
    """NGS beta SPCS2022 multizone-complete polygons, Michigan, 3857 -> 3078.

    The service stores Web Mercator (WGS 84 sphere-projected). Inverse
    spherical Mercator is exact; the result is treated numerically as NAD83
    lat/long (no datum shift applied) -- see RECON.md on what that costs."""
    p = os.path.join(RAW, "ngs_fs", "mi_native.json")
    d = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    out = {}
    for f in d["features"]:
        g = esri_rings_to_geom(f["geometry"]["rings"])
        g = transform(web_mercator_to_ll, g)
        out[f["attributes"]["ZoneCode"]] = (f["attributes"]["AbrvFull"],
                                            ll_to_m(g))
    return out


def ngs_statewide():
    p = os.path.join(RAW, "ngs_fs", "mi_statewide_native.json")
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        return None
    d = json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    f = d["features"][0]
    g = esri_rings_to_geom(f["geometry"]["rings"])
    return ll_to_m(transform(web_mercator_to_ll, g))

                        "DataCommon")
    r = shapefile.Reader(os.path.join(base, "MI_S_SPCS83"))
    g = unary_union([shape(s.__geo_interface__) for s in r.shapes()])

    def _render_sections(
        self,
        sections: tuple[ResultSection, ...] | None,
        warnings: str = NO_RESULT_WARNINGS,
    ) -> None:
        """Show a result, or ``None`` to empty the panel.

        Copy all follows the panel exactly: it is enabled when, and only when,
        there is something on screen to copy.

        The warnings field is driven from here rather than from ``convert``, so
        that it is emptied by the SAME call that empties the panel. Every route
        that discards a result - a control changing, a refusal, a fresh run
        starting - goes through this method, and a warnings field that outlived
        the numbers it described would be the stale-result failure of amendment
        #26 in a new place: the surveyor would read "none" beside a blank panel
        and take it as this point's answer.
        """
        self.panel.render_sections(sections)
        self.copy_all_button.setEnabled(sections is not None)
        self.warnings_label.setText(warnings)

    @property
    def sections(self) -> tuple[ResultSection, ...] | None:
        """The exact sections the panel last rendered, or None if it is empty.

        Read from the panel rather than kept beside it, so Copy all serialises
        what is on screen rather than a second copy of it that could go stale.
        """
        return self.panel.sections

    @property
    def value_labels(self) -> list[QLabel]:
        """The panel's value widgets, in screen order."""
        return self.panel.value_labels

    @property
    def copy_buttons(self) -> list[QToolButton]:
        """The panel's per-value copy buttons, in screen order."""
        return self.panel.copy_buttons

    def displayed_rows(self) -> tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]:
        """What the panel is showing, as (label, value) pairs in screen order."""
        return self.panel.displayed_rows()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Copying
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _set_clipboard(self, text: str) -> None:
        """The one route to the clipboard. Overridden in tests, which run
        headless and must not depend on a platform clipboard."""
        QGuiApplication.clipboard().setText(text)

    def copy_value(self, index: int) -> bool:
        """Put exactly one displayed value on the clipboard.

        The value string alone: no label, no unit, no trailing newline. It is
        pasted straight into a CAD prompt or a spreadsheet cell, and anything
        else in the buffer has to be deleted there.
        """
        if self.sections is None:
            # Nothing has been converted, so there is nothing to copy. Refused
            # rather than copying an empty string, which would silently destroy
            # whatever the user already had on the clipboard.
            return False
        self._set_clipboard(self.panel.values[index].text)
        return True

    def copy_all(self) -> bool:
        """Put the whole result on the clipboard, labels included.

        Serialises the *same* sections tuple the panel rendered, through
        ``results_model.single_point_clipboard_text``, so the screen and the
        clipboard cannot disagree about what the result contains.
        """
        if self.sections is None:
            return False
        self._set_clipboard(single_point_clipboard_text(self.sections))
        return True

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reporting
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def status_text(self, result: JobResult) -> str:
        if settings is None:
            # Convert is disabled in this state; reaching here would mean the
            # enablement logic and this method disagree, so say so rather than
            # running a half-specified job.
            self._report_failure(
                ValueError(
                    "The conversion settings are incomplete, so nothing was "
                    "run. Choose an input file, an output folder, both ends of "
                    "the conversion, the longitude sign convention when "
                    "geodetic coordinates are involved, the observation date "
                    "when a WGS 84 or ITRF frame is selected, and both "
                    "vertical datums when vertical mode is on."
                )
            )
            return False

        self.result = None
        self.written_files = {}
        self.last_failure = None
        self.model.set_result(None)
        self.open_folder_button.setEnabled(False)
        self._set_status("Converting…")

        # The computation is the long part; the writing is not, and the
        # overwrite prompt must not appear behind a wait cursor on a disabled
        # window. So only the run is wrapped.
        self.setEnabled(False)
        QApplication.setOverrideCursor(Qt.CursorShape.WaitCursor)
        try:
            result = run(settings)
        except htdp.HtdpRefusal as error:
            # NAMED, not left to the clause below (interim gate 2 of the WGS
            # 84 build, finding L4): an HTDP refusal subclasses neither
            # ValueError nor FrameMismatchError, so a handler narrowed to
            # those one day would let it escape with the window disabled and
            # the wait cursor up. Shown in full like every other refusal; the
            # table was emptied above, so no previous run is left beside it.
            failure = error
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - shown in full, then stopped
            failure = error
        else:
            failure = None
        finally:
            QApplication.restoreOverrideCursor()
            self.setEnabled(True)

        if failure is not None:
            self._report_failure(failure)
            return False

        try:
            written = self._write(result)
        except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - shown in full, then stopped
            self._report_failure(error)
            return False

        if written is None:
            return False

        self.result = result
        self.written_files = written
        self.model.set_result(result)
        self.table.resizeColumnsToContents()
        self._report_success(result)
        return True

    def _write(self, result: JobResult) -> dict[str, Path] | None:
        """Write the job's archive, asking before clobbering anything.

        ``exports.write_all`` refuses to overwrite unless told to. That refusal
        is answered by asking the user, never by passing ``overwrite=True``
        unconditionally — the whole point of the refusal is that a job written
        into the wrong folder must not quietly destroy the previous one.
        """
        try:
            return exports.write_all(result, overwrite=False)
        except exports.WriteError as error:
            existing = self._existing_outputs(result)
            if not existing:
                raise
            if not self._ask_overwrite(existing, error):
                self._set_status("Nothing was written. The existing files were kept.")
                return None
        return exports.write_all(result, overwrite=True)

    @staticmethod
    def _existing_outputs(result: JobResult) -> list[Path]:
        """Which of this job's destinations already hold a file.

        Asks ``exports`` rather than rebuilding the naming rule here, so this
        cannot drift out of step with what write_all actually produces. The
        paths are listed to the user by name, so the overwrite prompt says
        exactly what is at risk rather than "some files exist".
        """
        return [path for path in exports.destination_paths(result) if path.exists()]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reporting
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def status_text(self, result: JobResult) -> str:
        """"<n> points converted. <m> warnings." — the owner's wording.

        ``<m>`` counts the job's own warnings too (``results_model.
        warning_count``, work package W5): a job dated outside its WGS 84
        realization's period of use raises that warning once, about every
        point, and it is not in ``JobResult.warnings``.
        """
        return (
            f"{len(result.points)} points converted. "
            f"{warning_count(result)} warnings."
        )

    def _report_success(self, result: JobResult) -> None:
        warned = warning_count(result)
        self._set_status(
            self.status_text(result),
            style=AMBER if warned else "",
        )
        if warned:
"""Every CSV a default job writes, digested against v0.5.0. Frozen.

Closing gate, LOW 3. The ellipsoid-height feature rests on one promise: a job
that does not opt in produces exactly what the released program produced. That
promise was checked by hand at the gate — nine archives written twice, once in
a worktree at tag v0.5.0 and once at HEAD, all members digested — and the
evidence is committed at ``review/wp-e-byte-identity/``. But a captured
artifact does not fail when someone breaks it later, and the unit test that
carried the promise compared HEAD against HEAD: an unconditional regression, a
metre added to every height, left it green.

**These digests were computed by v0.5.0 itself**, not by the current code, so
they are a genuine cross-version pin. If a later change moves any byte of any
clean export or audit CSV on any of these nine ordinary jobs, this fails and
names the member.

Only the CSVs are pinned, and deliberately so: the job record embeds a
generation timestamp and the input and output paths, so its digest differs
between any two runs of identical code. What the record says is pinned by
content elsewhere, in the disclosure suites.

**The audit CSV is compared with its two DMS columns removed** (docs/DESIGN.md
amendment #66, the owner's instruction, 2026-09-03). ``Latitude (DMS)`` and
``Longitude (DMS)`` did not exist when v0.5.0 computed these digests, so the
raw member can no longer match them - and re-freezing the digests at HEAD
would have thrown away the cross-version property this file exists for.
Instead ``_without_columns`` parses the member and re-renders it through the
writer's own ``_render_csv`` with exactly those two headings dropped, and THAT
text is digested: every byte v0.5.0 wrote is still pinned to v0.5.0's own
digest, and the two new columns are pinned separately in
``tests/test_audit_dms.py``. ``test_the_stripping_is_exact`` establishes the
parse-and-render round trip reproduces an unmodified member byte for byte, so
the comparison is not passing through a lossy channel; and
``test_the_raw_member_no_longer_matches_but_the_stripped_one_does``
establishes the columns are really there - the stripped comparison would be
vacuous if nothing were stripped.
"""

"""Shared test helpers.

A job's deliverable is a single ZIP archive (docs/DESIGN.md amendment #17), so
tests that want to inspect what was actually written read members out of it
rather than opening loose files.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

import pytest


def archive_members(archive: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Every member of a written export, decoded, keyed by name.

    Reads through zipfile rather than trusting a path convention, so a test
    asserting "the export contains X" is asserting about the file on disk and
    not about how the test thinks the file was named.
    """
    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as handle:
        return {
            name: handle.read(name).decode("utf-8") for name in handle.namelist()
        }


def member_text(archive: Path, suffix: str) -> str:
    """The one member whose name ends with ``suffix``.

    Fails loudly on zero or several matches rather than silently picking one,
    since a test that reads the wrong member would still pass for the wrong
    reason.
    """
    members = archive_members(archive)
    matches = [name for name in members if name.endswith(suffix)]
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"expected exactly one member ending {suffix!r} in {archive.name}, "
            f"found {matches or 'none'} among {sorted(members)}"
        )
    return members[matches[0]]


def extract_member(archive: Path, suffix: str, into: Path) -> Path:
    """Write one member out to a real file and return its path.

    This is what the surveyor actually does with the export - unzip it, then
    hand the PNEZD file to CAD - so tests that check the export round-trips
    through this program's own reader go the same way rather than parsing the
    text in memory.
    """
    members = archive_members(archive)
    matches = [name for name in members if name.endswith(suffix)]
    if len(matches) != 1:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"expected exactly one member ending {suffix!r} in {archive.name}, "
            f"found {matches or 'none'} among {sorted(members)}"
        )
    into.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    destination = into / matches[0]
    destination.write_text(members[matches[0]], encoding="utf-8", newline="")
    return destination


@pytest.fixture
def read_member():
    """Fixture form of ``member_text``, for readability in test bodies."""
    return member_text


# The two record lines that carry an absolute path (michspc/fileio/report.py,
# "File" and "Folder"). Their 19-character label column is the report's own.
_PATH_LINE_LABELS = ("File               ", "Folder             ")


def record_root_normalised(text: str, root: Path) -> str:
    r"""``text`` with the temporary ``root`` replaced by ``<ROOT>``, and the
    remaining separators on the File and Folder lines written as ``/``.

    The record digests in the suite were frozen on Linux, where the path
    below the root is ``<ROOT>/job/in.csv``; on Windows the same record says
    ``<ROOT>\job\in.csv``. That difference is the platform's path spelling,
    not the program's output, so it is normalised - but ONLY on the two lines
    that carry a path, and only on lines that begin with the label followed
    by ``<ROOT>``: a backslash anywhere else in a record is still compared
    exactly. On Linux this is a no-op (a POSIX path has no backslash), so the
    frozen digests are compared there exactly as before.
    """
    text = text.replace(str(root), "<ROOT>")
    lines = text.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.startswith(tuple(label + "<ROOT>" for label in _PATH_LINE_LABELS)):
            lines[index] = line.replace("\\", "/")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def square(x0, y0, x1, y1, clockwise=True):
    ring = ((x0, y0), (x0, y1), (x1, y1), (x1, y0), (x0, y0))
    return ring if clockwise else tuple(reversed(ring))


def which(county_set: CountySet, lon, lat) -> list[str]:
    return [c.fips for c in county_set.containing(lon, lat)]

# ==========================================================================


def test_holes_and_islands_by_even_odd_over_every_ring():
    # A 10x10 square with a 2x2 hole at (4..6, 4..6) and a separate 1x1 island
    # at (20..21, 0..1). Even-odd over all three rings: the hole is outside
    # (two crossings), the island inside (one), no ring marked as a hole.
    rings = (square(0, 0, 10, 10), square(4, 4, 6, 6, clockwise=False), square(20, 0, 21, 1))
    county = PreparedCounty.build(County("26999", "Test", rings))
    assert county.contains(1.0, 1.0)  # in the square, outside the hole
    assert not county.contains(5.0, 5.0)  # in the hole
    assert county.contains(20.5, 0.5)  # on the island
    assert not county.contains(15.0, 0.5)  # between square and island
    assert even_odd_contains(rings, 5.0, 5.0) is False
    assert even_odd_contains(rings, 1.0, 1.0) is True


def test_ring_orientation_does_not_matter():
    for clockwise in (True, False):
        county = PreparedCounty.build(County("26999", "T", (square(0, 0, 1, 1, clockwise),)))
        assert county.contains(0.5, 0.5)
        assert not county.contains(1.5, 0.5)


# Four unit squares meeting at (1, 1):
#
#     C (0..1, 1..2) | D (1..2, 1..2)
#     ---------------+---------------
#     A (0..1, 0..1) | B (1..2, 0..1)
#
# B and D are walked counter-clockwise, A and C clockwise, so each shared edge
# is stored in opposite directions by its two owners - the case the canonical
# edge order exists for.
QUAD = CountySet(
    [
        County("26001", "A", (square(0, 0, 1, 1),)),
        County("26003", "B", (square(1, 0, 2, 1, clockwise=False),)),
        County("26005", "C", (square(0, 1, 1, 2),)),
        County("26007", "D", (square(1, 1, 2, 2, clockwise=False),)),
    ],
    source="synthetic squares",
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "lon, lat, expected, why",
    [
        (1.0, 0.5, ["26003"], "on the A|B north-south line: the county EAST (B)"),
        (1.0, 1.5, ["26007"], "on the C|D north-south line: east (D)"),
        (0.5, 1.0, ["26005"], "on the A/C east-west line: the county NORTH (C)"),
        (1.5, 1.0, ["26007"], "on the B/D east-west line: north (D)"),
        (1.0, 1.0, ["26007"], "on the four-way corner: north-east (D)"),
        (0.0, 0.5, ["26001"], "on A's west outline: east of it is A"),
        (2.0, 0.5, [], "on B's east outline: east of it is outside"),
        (0.5, 0.0, ["26001"], "on A's south outline: north of it is A"),
        (0.5, 2.0, [], "on C's north outline: north of it is outside"),
        (0.0, 0.0, ["26001"], "A's south-west corner: north-east is A"),
        (2.0, 2.0, [], "D's north-east corner: north-east is outside"),
        (0.5, 0.5, ["26001"], "plainly inside A"),
    ],
)
def test_the_on_line_rule_east_then_north(lon, lat, expected, why):
    assert which(QUAD, lon, lat) == expected, why


def test_a_sloped_shared_edge_gives_an_exact_on_edge_point_to_one_county():
    # Two triangles sharing the sloped edge (0,0)-(1,3), walked in opposite
    # directions. The on-edge point at latitude 1 is longitude 1/3, computed
    # by the canonical formula itself so it is EXACTLY on the edge as the code
    # sees it: x = 0 + (1 - 0) * (1 - 0) / (3 - 0).
    west = County("26001", "W", (((0.0, 0.0), (-1.0, 3.0), (1.0, 3.0), (0.0, 0.0)),))
    east = County("26003", "E", (((0.0, 0.0), (1.0, 3.0), (2.0, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0)),))
    pair = CountySet([west, east], source="synthetic")
    x = 0.0 + (1.0 - 0.0) * (1.0 - 0.0) / (3.0 - 0.0)
    assert which(pair, x, 1.0) == ["26003"]  # on the line: the county east of it
    assert which(pair, math.nextafter(x, -1.0), 1.0) == ["26001"]


# ==========================================================================
# The rule on the real county lines.
# ==========================================================================


def _exact_on_edge_point(a, b):
    """A point the canonical crossing test sees as EXACTLY on edge a-b: the
    canonical lower endpoint first, latitude halfway, longitude by the same
    interpolation formula the program uses."""
    (xa, ya), (xb, yb) = sorted([a, b], key=lambda p: (p[1], p[0]))
    lat = (ya + yb) / 2.0
    return xa + (lat - ya) * (xb - xa) / (yb - ya), lat


def test_every_shared_county_line_point_lands_in_exactly_one_of_its_two_counties(shipped):
    """All 30,871 shared edges: a point exactly on each one - for a sloped edge
    the canonical interpolation at mid-latitude, for a horizontal one the
    midpoint - belongs to exactly one county, and it is one of the edge's two
    owners. The partition the even-odd rule promises, held on TIGER's own
    vertices rather than on a picture of them. (The endpoints are the vertex
    test's business: an endpoint can be a three-county junction, or sit on
    Michigan's outline where north-east of it is outside.)"""
    bad = []
    count = 0
    for a, b, owners in geo.edges_with_owners():
        if len(owners) != 2:
            continue
        if a[1] != b[1]:
            points = [_exact_on_edge_point(a, b)]
        else:
            points = [((a[0] + b[0]) / 2.0, a[1])]
        for lon, lat in points:
            got = which(shipped, lon, lat)
            if len(got) != 1 or got[0] not in owners:
                bad.append((lon, lat, sorted(owners), got))
        count += 1
    assert count == 30871
    assert not bad, bad[:5]


def test_a_point_on_the_eaton_ingham_line_goes_to_ingham_the_county_east(shipped):
    # Eaton (26045) is west of Ingham (26065); their common line is a
    # north-south range line near 84.60 W. On it, the rule says east: Ingham.
    shared = [
        (a, b)
        for a, b, owners in geo.edges_with_owners()
        if owners == {"26045", "26065"} and a[1] != b[1]
    ]
    assert len(shared) > 10
    for a, b in shared:
        lon, lat = _exact_on_edge_point(a, b)
        assert which(shipped, lon, lat) == ["26065"]
        # A centimetre either side, by the independent test: west is Eaton.
        assert geo.plain_even_odd(shipped.by_fips("26045").rings, lon - 1e-7, lat)
        assert geo.plain_even_odd(shipped.by_fips("26065").rings, lon + 1e-7, lat)


def test_a_point_on_the_alcona_iosco_line_goes_to_alcona_the_county_north(shipped):
    # Alcona (26001) is north of Iosco (26069); TIGER stores much of their
    # line as exactly horizontal edges (near 44.512 N). On each: north, Alcona.
    horizontal = [
        (a, b)
        for a, b, owners in geo.edges_with_owners()
        if owners == {"26001", "26069"} and a[1] == b[1]
    ]
    assert len(horizontal) > 10
    for a, b in horizontal:
        lon = (a[0] + b[0]) / 2.0
        assert which(shipped, lon, a[1]) == ["26001"]


def test_every_multi_county_vertex_goes_to_its_north_east_county(shipped):
    """The 115 vertices where three or four counties meet. Expected county:
    the one an independent even-odd test finds a hair north-east of the vertex
    (1e-7 degree east, 1e-12 north - the rule's 'east, then a far smaller step
    north'; the ratio must be smaller than any incident edge's slope, or a
    nearly-horizontal line leaving the vertex north-eastward would be crossed,
    which a ratio of 1e-2 was measured to do at 46.158691 N 86.615601 W)."""
    owners_at: dict = {}
    for a, b, owners in geo.edges_with_owners():
        for v in (a, b):
            owners_at.setdefault(v, set()).update(owners)
    corners = [v for v, o in owners_at.items() if len(o) >= 3]
    assert len(corners) == 115
    for lon, lat in corners:
        got = which(shipped, lon, lat)
        expected = [
            c.fips
            for c in shipped.counties
            if geo.plain_even_odd(c.rings, lon + 1e-7, lat + 1e-12)
        ]
        assert len(got) == 1 and got == expected, (lon, lat, got, expected)

def test_tiger_topology_every_edge_used_once_or_twice_never_twice_by_one_county():
    uses = geo.edge_use_counts()
    assert set(uses.values()) == {1, 2}
    assert sum(1 for n in uses.values() if n == 1) == 10720  # Michigan's outline
    for county in geo.county_document()["counties"]:
        seen = set()
        for ring in county["rings"]:
            for a, b in zip(ring[:-1], ring[1:]):
                key = frozenset((tuple(a), tuple(b)))
                assert key not in seen, county["name"]
                seen.add(key)


def test_no_point_of_a_statewide_grid_is_in_two_counties(shipped):
    # A 0.02-degree grid over the whole box TIGER's Michigan spans
    # (41.69-48.31 N, 90.42-82.12 W): about 137,000 points.
    in_two = []
    inside = 0
    lat = 41.69
    while lat <= 48.31:
        lon = -90.42
        while lon <= -82.12:
            got = shipped.containing(lon, lat)
            inside += len(got) == 1
            if len(got) > 1:
                in_two.append((lat, lon, [c.name for c in got]))
            lon += 0.02
        lat += 0.02
    assert not in_two, in_two[:5]
    assert inside > 60000  # Michigan, its water included, is most of the box

    random points, the binned answer equals the all-edges count and the
    suite's independent even-odd test, for every county whose box comes within

            ys = [p[1] for r in c.rings for p in r]
            if min(xs) - 0.1 <= lon <= max(xs) + 0.1 and min(ys) - 0.1 <= lat <= max(ys) + 0.1:

def _independent_county(lat, lon):
    return [
        (c["fips"], c["name"])
        for c in geo.county_document()["counties"]
        if geo.plain_even_odd(c["rings"], lon, lat)
    ]


def test_the_zone_is_chosen_at_the_nad83_pivot_where_the_two_positions_straddle_a_zone_line():
    result = run(
        settings(geodetic_frame=WGS84_G2296, observation_date=DATE),
        source((7, *STRADDLE, None)),
    )
    (point,) = result.points
    pivot = (point.conversion.latitude, point.conversion.longitude)
    assert pivot != STRADDLE
    assert _independent_county(*STRADDLE) == [("26011", "Arenac")]
    assert _independent_county(*pivot) == [("26063", "Huron")]
    assert point.auto_zone.zone is MI_SOUTH
    assert (point.auto_zone.county_fips, point.auto_zone.county_name) == ("26063", "Huron")

    fixed = run(
        settings(
            geodetic_frame=WGS84_G2296,
            observation_date=DATE,
            target_zone=MI_SOUTH,
            auto_frame=None,
        ),
        source((7, *STRADDLE, None)),
    )
    assert_bit_identical(point, fixed.points[0])

    )

    )


def _frame_label(frame: object) -> str:
    code = getattr(frame, "code", None)
    return code if isinstance(code, str) else repr(frame)


def _require_no_stray_frame_fields(settings: JobSettings) -> None:
    """Refuse a frame field this job's direction never reads, by name.

    The 0.7.0 closing gate's stray-zone MEDIUM, applied to the two frame
    fields (docs/PLAN-wgs84.md section 3.5, "from the lead's W2 probe";
    interim gate 1 of the WGS 84 build, finding I1). A ``ZONE_TO_ZONE`` job -
    or a ``VERTICAL_ONLY`` job reading State Plane coordinates - given a
    ``geodetic_frame`` of WGS84(G2296) runs, ignores it, and converts
    correctly; but the field is a statement about where the job's positions
    are, the job never made that statement true, and a later surface that
    printed it would describe a frame nothing was in. ``target_geodetic_frame``
    is read only by ``GEODETIC_TO_GEODETIC``.

    ``geodetic_frame`` is DEFAULTED to NAD83(2011), so the test is "differs
    from the default", in value: a caller that rebuilt the default record
    field for field has stated nothing. Both interface tabs already set the
    field only when a side is geodetic (``controls.geodetic_frame_for``), so
    this refuses nothing they build.
    """
    if (
        settings.direction is not Direction.GEODETIC_TO_GEODETIC
        and settings.target_geodetic_frame is not None
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"A {settings.direction.name} job was given target_geodetic_frame="
            f"{_frame_label(settings.target_geodetic_frame)}, which only a "
            f"{Direction.GEODETIC_TO_GEODETIC.name} job reads: this "
            f"direction's one geodetic end, if it has one, is geodetic_frame. "
            f"A second frame stated here would be one the job record could "
            f"print and the conversion never used. Pass "
            f"target_geodetic_frame=None."
        )
    if not _reads_geodetic_frame(settings) and settings.geodetic_frame != NAD83_2011:
        reading = (
            "both ends are zones"
            if settings.direction is Direction.ZONE_TO_ZONE
            else "the input is State Plane coordinates and nothing is written "
            "as latitude and longitude"
        )
        raise ValueError(
            f"A {settings.direction.name} job was given geodetic_frame="
            f"{_frame_label(settings.geodetic_frame)}, which this job never "
            f"reads: {reading}, and each zone carries its own frame. The "
            f"conversion would run in the zones' frame and ignore the field, "
            f"while the field states that this job's positions are in "
            f"{_frame_label(settings.geodetic_frame)} - a frame nothing in the "
            f"job is in. Refused here rather than ignored, as a stray zone is. "
            f"Leave geodetic_frame at its default, {NAD83_2011.code}."
        )


def _require_a_registered_frame_path(
    settings: JobSettings,
) -> FrameTransformation | None:
    """The frame path this job's rows will apply - or a refusal, before the file is read.

    ``convert.project_point``, ``convert.zone_to_geodetic`` and the other
    conversion functions each pass their own ends through
    ``frames.require_frame_path``, so a cross-frame job could never produce a
    wrong coordinate. What it could do before this gate existed is read the
    file, convert forty rows, and fail on the forty-first only because that is
    when the loop reached it - a whole-job refusal announced as though it were
    about one point. It is about the settings, so it fires here.

    The pair this checks is the one the settings alone can put in disagreement:
    ``geodetic_frame`` names the frame a geodetic END is in, and the zone (or
    the second geodetic frame) at the other end carries its own:

    * ``GEODETIC_TO_ZONE`` - the file's latitudes and longitudes are read as
      ``geodetic_frame`` and projected into ``target_zone``;
    * ``ZONE_TO_GEODETIC`` - ``source_zone``'s coordinates are inverted into
      the zone's own frame and written out in ``geodetic_frame``. A 2022-zone
      job left on the NAD83(2011) default refuses: there is no published
      NATRF2022 <-> NAD83(2011) path, and writing NATRF2022 positions under a
      NAD83(2011) label is one to two metres, invisible in the numbers;
    * ``GEODETIC_TO_GEODETIC`` - ``geodetic_frame`` to ``target_geodetic_frame``,
      and only across a registered NON-identity path (plan decision D7): the
      same frame at both ends converts nothing, and is refused rather than
      run as a conversion that changed no number;
    * ``VERTICAL_ONLY`` with a GEODETIC input - ``convert.pivot_path``: the
      frame's identity when it is plate-fixed, its HTDP path to NAD83(2011)
      when it is time-dependent (plan decision D8), and the bare WGS 84 label
      refused by name. Until the 0.7.0 closing gate this direction was skipped
      entirely, and a ``VERTICAL_ONLY`` job stating ``WGS84`` certified a NAVD
      88 elevation under a record reading "Reference frame WGS84". The same
      function is the per-point gate in ``convert.geodetic_position``
      (interim gate 1, finding L5), so the two cannot choose different paths.

    ``ZONE_TO_ZONE`` and ``VERTICAL_ONLY`` with a zone input are not checked
    here and return None: every end is a zone, and ``convert_point`` gates the
    pair itself.

    The refusal is ``frames``' own, raised by ``require_frame_path`` and
    propagated UNTOUCHED - it already names both frames, the metre-scale stake,
    NGS's unpublished transformation and the ways out, and wrapping it would
    hide the ``FrameMismatchError`` subclasses callers are told to catch.

    **Since work package W3 a registered path is an APPLIED one.** The record
    found here is returned, and ``run`` hands it to every row, so the
    observation date the path requires is decided from the same record the
    rows apply. It still passes ``convert.require_an_applicable_path``, the
    single point where a path whose method this program cannot run is
"""Work package W4 of the WGS 84 build: no same-frame job moves by a byte.

W4 (docs/PLAN-wgs84.md section 3.6) adds the FRAME TRANSFORMATION block to
the job record, conditional columns to the audit CSV, a geodetic-to-geodetic
branch to every output, and frame-aware wording to the sentences a
transformation would otherwise make false. Every one of those is conditional
on a frame transformation having run. This file is the proof that the
condition holds the other way: a job with no transformation writes what it
wrote before W4, every member, every byte.

**The digests below were computed by the code BEFORE W4** - commit 8201968
(the W3 commit), with ``_written`` exactly as it stands here - so this is a
cross-version pin of the kind ``tests/test_orthometric_regression.py`` is
(whose eighteen v0.5.0 digests remain the floor, untouched). That file
covers nine zone-input jobs and no record; this one adds one job of every
direction that has a geodetic end or a record branch W4 touched, and digests
the RECORD too, with its two run-dependent parts normalised: the
``Generated`` timestamp, and the temporary folder every path sits under.

Jobs, and the W4 branch each one holds closed:

* ``z2z`` - zone to zone, with an outside-zone warning: the WARNINGS section
  (job-level warnings are W4's).
* ``g2z`` - NAD83(2011) geodetic to MI-C, positive west, a blank Z: the
  ELEVATIONS "does not depend on elevation" paragraph, and the OUTPUT
  section's Reference frame line.
* ``z2g_ellipsoid`` - MI-S to NAD83(2011) geodetic, ELLIPSOID heights,
  horizontal: the ELLIPSOID HEIGHT CONVERSION block's "exactly as supplied"
  sentence, the DD/DMS members and the audit CSV's ellipsoid headings.
* ``g2z_hv`` - geodetic in, horizontal and vertical NGVD 29 to NAVD 88: the
  vertical blocks beside the geodetic input block.
* ``vo_zone`` and ``vo_geodetic`` - vertical only, on a zone and on
  NAD83(2011) positions with ellipsoid heights: the two vertical-only
  records, which W4 does not alter.
"""

"""Z0: choose and capture the NCAT zone anchors Auto zone is pinned to.

    py -I review/autozone-z0/capture_anchors.py select   # choose the points
    py -I review/autozone-z0/capture_anchors.py query    # ask NCAT, live

``select`` picks, for each of Michigan's 83 counties, the land point deepest
inside it: a 41 x 41 grid over the county's bounding box, kept only where the
point is inside the county (data/mi_counties_tiger2025.json) AND on land (inside
one of NGS's land-only SPCS2022 polygons, review/autozone-r0/raw/ngs_fs/
mi_4269.json), scored by its distance to the nearest edge of the county's own
polygon, best kept. Being deep inside its county puts it far from every zone
line. Written to work/anchor_points.json.

``query`` asks NGS NCAT which zone it picks for each chosen point, plus the
recon's 14 Great Lakes water points and 13 Keweenaw-to-Isle-Royale transect
points for SPCS 83 (the recon asked those for SPCS2022 only):

* SPCS 83: production REST, https://geodesy.noaa.gov/api/ncat/llh, NAD83(2011)
  in and out, no spcZone - NCAT picks the zone (RECON.md section 5.1);
* SPCS2022: the beta web app's JSF form, NATRF2022 epoch 2020.00 in and out,
  zone list left on "Auto Pick (default zone)" (RECON.md section 5.1; the form
  code is review/autozone-r0/probe_ncat.py's, reused unchanged).

Every response is saved raw under raw/ with its SHA-256 in
work/anchor_ncat.json. Stdlib only, plus the repository's own michspc package
(for the point-in-polygon of the selection step; NCAT decides the answers).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import math
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "review" / "autozone-r0"))

from michspc.spc.autozone import County, PreparedCounty  # noqa: E402

RAW = HERE / "raw"
WORK = HERE / "work"
R0 = REPO / "review" / "autozone-r0"


def local_metres(lat0: float):
    """Metres per degree of latitude and of longitude at lat0 (GRS 80)."""
    a, f = 6378137.0, 1 / 298.257222101
    e2 = f * (2 - f)
    s = math.sin(math.radians(lat0))
    w = math.sqrt(1 - e2 * s * s)
    m = a * (1 - e2) / w**3  # meridian radius
    n = a / w  # prime vertical radius
    return math.radians(1) * m, math.radians(1) * n * math.cos(math.radians(lat0))


def seg_distance(px, py, ax, ay, bx, by, my, mx):
    ax, ay, bx, by = (ax - px) * mx, (ay - py) * my, (bx - px) * mx, (by - py) * my
    dx, dy = bx - ax, by - ay
    L = dx * dx + dy * dy
    t = 0.0 if L == 0 else max(0.0, min(1.0, -(ax * dx + ay * dy) / L))
    return math.hypot(ax + t * dx, ay + t * dy)


def load_counties():
    doc = json.loads((REPO / "data" / "mi_counties_tiger2025.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return [
        County(c["fips"], c["name"], tuple(tuple((x, y) for x, y in r) for r in c["rings"]))
        for c in doc["counties"]
    ]


def load_ngs_land():
    doc = json.loads((R0 / "raw" / "ngs_fs" / "mi_4269.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return [
        PreparedCounty.build(
            County(
                f["attributes"]["ZoneCode"],
                f["attributes"]["AbrvFull"],
                tuple(tuple((x, y) for x, y in r) for r in f["geometry"]["rings"]),
            )
        )
        for f in doc["features"]
    ]


def select():
    counties = load_counties()
    land = load_ngs_land()
    out = []
    for c in counties:
        pc = PreparedCounty.build(c)
        ring_edges = [e for r in c.rings for e in zip(r[:-1], r[1:])]
        best = None
        n = 41
        for i in range(1, n):
            for j in range(1, n):
                x = pc.min_longitude + (pc.max_longitude - pc.min_longitude) * i / n
                y = pc.min_latitude + (pc.max_latitude - pc.min_latitude) * j / n
                if not pc.contains(x, y):
                    continue
                if not any(z.contains(x, y) for z in land):
                    continue
                my, mx = local_metres(y)
                d = min(seg_distance(x, y, a[0], a[1], b[0], b[1], my, mx) for a, b in ring_edges)
                if best is None or d > best[0]:
                    best = (d, round(y, 6), round(x, 6))
        if best is None:
            raise SystemExit(f"no land grid point inside {c.name}")
        out.append({"tag": f"COUNTY {c.fips} {c.name}", "fips": c.fips, "lat": best[1],
                    "lon": best[2], "depth_m": round(best[0], 1)})
        print(c.fips, c.name, best)
    WORK.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (WORK / "anchor_points.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


def recon_extra_points():
    """The recon's water and Keweenaw transect points, asked for SPCS2022 only."""
    rows = json.loads((R0 / "work" / "r2_ncat_22.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return [
        {"tag": r["tag"], "lat": r["lat"], "lon": r["lon"]}
        for r in rows
        if r["tag"].split()[0] in ("WATER", "KEWEENAW_TRANSECT")
    ]


def query():
    import probe_ncat  # review/autozone-r0/probe_ncat.py: fetch, form code

    probe_ncat.RAW = str(RAW)
    RAW.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    points = json.loads((WORK / "anchor_points.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    # Isle Royale's land, the one county-part the deepest-point rule cannot
    # reach (Keweenaw's deepest land point is on the mainland). Inland on the
    # island, about 10 km from 47.65 N; checked as land in the suite.
    points.append({"tag": "ISLE_ROYALE_LAND", "fips": "26083", "lat": 48.0, "lon": -88.8})
    extra = recon_extra_points()

    results = {"spcs83": [], "spcs2022": []}
    for i, pt in enumerate(points + extra):
        q = urllib.parse.urlencode({"lat": "%.8f" % pt["lat"], "lon": "%.8f" % pt["lon"],
                                    "inDatum": "NAD83(2011)", "outDatum": "NAD83(2011)"})
        body = probe_ncat.fetch(probe_ncat.PROD + "?" + q)
        name = "z0_spcs83_%03d.json" % i
        (RAW / name).write_bytes(body)
        zone = json.loads(body).get("spcZone")
        results["spcs83"].append(dict(pt, ncat_zone=zone, raw=name,
                                      sha256=hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()))
        print("83", i, pt["tag"], zone)
        time.sleep(0.4)

    probe_ncat.PREFIX = "z0_"
    res22 = probe_ncat.run22(points)
    results["spcs2022"] = res22
    (WORK / "anchor_ncat.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1) + "\n",
                                           encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    {"select": select, "query": query}[sys.argv[1]]()

76 COUNTY 26153 Schoolcraft MI U21E-261014 (Multizone complete)
77 COUNTY 26155 Shiawassee MI L21F-261003 (Multizone complete)
78 COUNTY 26157 Tuscola MI L25S-261004 (Multizone complete)
79 COUNTY 26159 Van Buren MI L41Z-261007 (Multizone complete)
80 COUNTY 26161 Washtenaw MI L11A-261001 (Multizone complete)
81 COUNTY 26163 Wayne MI L15D-261002 (Multizone complete)
82 COUNTY 26165 Wexford MI L55W-261010 (Multizone complete)
83 ISLE_ROYALE_LAND MI U61K-261018 (Multizone complete)
        geoid.default_grid(factors_model) if factors_model is not None else None
    )

    # The geoid-to-geoid conversion's two grids, loaded once per job exactly
    # as the factors grid above is. None on every job that is not a swap -
    # including the same model stated on both sides, which is the ordinary
    # identity job with no swap step.
    swap_models = geoid_swap_models(settings, transformation)
    swap_grids = (
        _GeoidSwapGrids(
            source_model=swap_models[0],
            target_model=swap_models[1],
            source_grid=geoid.default_grid(swap_models[0]),
            target_grid=geoid.default_grid(swap_models[1]),
        )
        if swap_models is not None
        else None
    )

    # The VERTCON pair, loaded ONCE per job exactly as the geoid grid above is
    # - not per row (two 2.4 MB files re-read per point), and NOT for an
    # identity: an identity applies no grid, apply_shift refuses a grid value
    # for one, and a NAVD 88 to NAVD 88 job must succeed with the VERTCON
    # files absent entirely.
    vertcon_grids = (
        vertcon.default_grids()
        if transformation is not None and not transformation.is_identity
        else None
    )

    # The county polygons, read and authenticated once per process, and only
    # for an Auto job: a fixed-zone job never touches the county file, so it
    # converts with the file absent exactly as it always did.
    county_set = (
        county_file.default_counties() if settings.target_zone is AUTO_ZONE else None
    )

    points: list[ConvertedPoint] = []
    unplaced: list[_UnplacedPoint] = []
    for row in parsed.rows:
        try:
            points.append(
                _convert_row(
                    row,
                    settings,
                    grid,
                    transformation,
                    vertcon_grids,
                    swap_grids,
                    frame_path=frame_path,
                    epoch=epoch,
                    county_set=county_set,
                )
            )
        except _AutoZoneUnplaced as signal:
            # Collected, not skipped: the loop runs on only so the refusal
            # below can name EVERY row Auto cannot place, and then the whole
            # job is refused (the house rule; plan L5).
            unplaced.append(signal.point)
    if unplaced:
        raise _unplaced_points_refusal(unplaced, county_set)

    return JobResult(
        settings=settings,
        points=tuple(points),
        # The digest of the bytes the parser consumed, and nothing else. None
        # when the rows arrived already parsed - see JobResult.input_sha256.
        input_sha256=parsed.sha256,
        input_row_count=len(parsed.rows),
        skipped_blank_lines=parsed.skipped_blank_lines,
        # The NAME of the model the factors were actually computed from, not
        # the record: JobResult's contract predates the registry and
        # report.py resolves the record back through geoid_model_by_name.
        # For every pre-existing call shape this is settings.geoid_model's
        # own name; since the per-side feature it is the factors side's, so
        # a job whose only model is input-side (geoid_model=None,
        # source_geoid_model=GEOID18) names the grid its factors really
        # came from rather than claiming no geoid was applied.
        geoid_model=(
            factors_model.name if factors_model is not None else None
        ),
        job_warnings=job_warnings,
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _GeoidSwapGrids:
    """A swap job's two models with their loaded grids - run()'s per-job
    wiring, handed to ``_convert_row`` so the tiles are read once per job,
    not per row."""

    source_model: geoid.GeoidModel
    target_model: geoid.GeoidModel
    source_grid: object
    target_grid: object
